themes.name: Should bankruptcy courts exercise equitable discretion to resolve statutory gaps, or should clearer statutory rules constrain that discretion?
themes.definition: This question addresses the tension between flexible, context-sensitive adjudication and predictable, uniform application of the Bankruptcy Code.

themes.name: Do bankruptcy courts and specialized venues such as Delaware courts improve reorganization outcomes through institutional expertise and competition?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether venue choice, court specialization, and institutional design affect efficiency, consistency, stakeholder protection, and case results.

themes.name: Should Chapter 11 use substantially different procedures for small businesses than for complex large corporate debtors?
themes.definition: This question asks whether procedural simplification and tailored safeguards can make reorganization accessible to small firms without reducing creditor protection.

themes.name: Do prevailing economic and legal theories of bankruptcy accurately describe how participants behave in complex reorganizations?
themes.definition: This question tests whether formal models of incentives, value maximization, creditor coordination, and priority correspond to empirical practice and observed outcomes.

themes.name: Have statutory reforms such as BAPCPA achieved their intended objectives, or have they created new obstacles to business reorganization?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether changes to Chapter 11 administration, creditor rights, and debtor protections improve restructuring outcomes or produce unintended consequences.

themes.name: Does Chapter 11 preserve viable going-concern value better than liquidation or asset redeployment?
themes.definition: This question examines whether formal reorganization can distinguish and preserve economically viable firms without inefficiently prolonging cases whose assets should be liquidated.

themes.name: Who should control a distressed company during Chapter 11: incumbent managers, secured creditors, other creditor classes, or the court?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how control rights should shift among managers, shareholders, creditors, and court-appointed or statutory actors as insolvency develops.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy distributions preserve pre-bankruptcy priority and property rights or redistribute value to support reorganization?
themes.definition: This question addresses when Chapter 11 should honor state-law, contractual, and prepetition entitlements and when it may legitimately depart from them.

themes.name: How should secured-creditor foreclosure rights be balanced against the debtor’s opportunity to reorganize?
themes.definition: This question examines the legal limits on enforcement by secured lenders when foreclosure could destroy going-concern value or prevent a successful restructuring.

themes.name: Do debtor-in-possession financing arrangements improperly transfer value from existing creditors to secured lenders?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether DIP financing terms, liens, and administrative priorities fairly allocate restructuring value and risk between new lenders and existing claimants.

themes.name: Should private contracts be permitted to modify statutory bankruptcy rights and constrain future restructuring?
themes.definition: This question compares mandatory bankruptcy rules with contractual freedom in determining whether prepetition agreements should control restructuring, enforcement, and voting outcomes.

themes.name: Does collective bankruptcy better resolve creditor coordination problems than allowing individual enforcement or competition after default?
themes.definition: This question examines whether centralizing claims and remedies improves recoveries and fairness when creditors have conflicting incentives to seize assets or negotiate separately.

themes.name: How should courts interpret ambiguous Bankruptcy Code provisions when textual rules conflict with equitable or economically functional outcomes?
themes.definition: This question concerns the appropriate role of statutory text, precedent, historical practice, judicial discretion, and broader bankruptcy policy in resolving unsettled issues.

themes.name: Do Chapter 11’s administrative, professional, and procedural costs materially reduce creditor recoveries and restructuring efficiency?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether court oversight, professional fees, delay, and accelerated procedures improve case administration enough to justify their effects on distributions.

themes.name: Does Chapter 11 provide adequate protection and participation rights to unsecured creditors?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether unsecured creditors can meaningfully monitor, vote, negotiate, and recover value despite the influence of secured lenders and the debtor.

themes.name: Should tort claims and other noncontractual claims survive reorganization or a going-concern sale?
themes.definition: This question examines whether bankruptcy should discharge, centralize, estimate, or preserve individual claims that are difficult to value or that implicate nondebtor parties.

themes.name: Should directors’ fiduciary duties shift toward creditors when a corporation becomes insolvent or approaches insolvency?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how financial distress changes corporate decision-making obligations and the legal relationship between managers, shareholders, creditors, and the firm.

themes.name: Do bankruptcy rules create strategic incentives that undermine efficient restructuring?
themes.definition: This question examines whether leverage, claim trading, technical objections, filing decisions, contractual gaps, and creditor-specific strategies produce opportunistic rather than value-maximizing behavior.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy procedures be tailored to the size, complexity, and capital structure of the distressed business?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether broad categorical Chapter 11 rules adequately serve large public companies, complex debtors, small businesses, and factually diverse cases.

themes.name: Is formal Chapter 11 preferable to out-of-court workouts, government intervention, or other restructuring mechanisms?
themes.definition: This question compares court-supervised reorganization with private and regulatory alternatives in light of coordination costs, bankruptcy costs, creditor protection, and going-concern value.

themes.name: Do Chapter 11 confirmation and distribution procedures allocate enterprise value fairly among creditor classes and equityholders?
themes.definition: This question examines valuation, voting, plan treatment, bargaining power, and departures from ordinary priority in determining who receives the reorganized firm’s value.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy courts use flexible standards or bright-line rules to police preferential and abusive treatment?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether judicial discretion and case-specific safeguards produce better outcomes than predictable rules restricting creditor or debtor advantages.

themes.name: Do disclosure, valuation, and risk-allocation rules give bankruptcy participants enough information to make efficient restructuring decisions?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether parties can accurately assess enterprise value, restructuring risk, claim recoveries, and proposed transactions under existing Chapter 11 procedures.

themes.name: Should legislative or institutional reform replace or substantially redesign Chapter 11?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether empirical evidence, changing financial markets, doctrinal inconsistency, and practical gaps justify statutory amendment, institutional redesign, or replacement of the current system.

themes.name: Can specialized courts, trustees, commissions, or neutral intervenors improve outcomes in complex bankruptcy cases?
themes.definition: This question examines whether independent or specialized institutional actors can reduce conflicts, improve oversight, and produce more legitimate and efficient resolutions than ordinary case administration.

themes.name: Should Chapter 11 prioritize creditor recoveries over preserving a distressed firm as a going concern?
themes.definition: This question examines how reorganization law should trade off creditor-value maximization against preserving viable businesses, employment, and broader stakeholder value.

themes.name: Does the absolute priority rule appropriately limit existing equity holders’ ability to retain ownership in reorganization?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether confirmation rules, including the new-value doctrine, properly constrain equity retention when creditors are not paid in full.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy law permit distressed firms to modify or shed nonbankruptcy contractual and statutory obligations?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether Chapter 11 should displace obligations arising under contract, state law, or other legal regimes when doing so facilitates reorganization.

themes.name: Should private creditor bargains control in bankruptcy, or may mandatory bankruptcy rules override them?
themes.definition: This question evaluates when contractual allocations of priority, voting, enforcement, and recovery rights should be enforced or limited by collective insolvency law.

themes.name: Do secured-creditor rights and DIP financing arrangements give lenders excessive control over Chapter 11 reorganizations?
themes.definition: This question examines whether liens, financing terms, and lender-imposed conditions allow secured creditors to control corporate decisions beyond what is justified by their legal entitlements.

themes.name: How should bankruptcy distribute value when secured and unsecured creditors assert competing claims to the same estate or collateral?
themes.definition: This question addresses priority, valuation, and distribution rules governing conflicts among secured, unsecured, contingent, and other creditor groups.

themes.name: Do bankruptcy classification and voting rules produce fair and economically justified distributions among creditor classes?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how legal classification of claims shapes bargaining power, plan approval, and the allocation of estate value.

themes.name: Are Chapter 11’s procedural protections adequate to enable meaningful creditor participation?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether notice, disclosure, voting, evidentiary access, and other procedural safeguards allow creditors and investors to protect their interests effectively.

themes.name: Who should control key decisions in an insolvency proceeding: managers, creditors, equity holders, trustees, or the court?
themes.definition: This question examines the allocation of authority over financing, asset sales, plan design, litigation, and other major reorganization decisions.

themes.name: Does bankruptcy-court discretion improve reorganization outcomes, or does unguided discretion create unpredictability and favoritism?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the proper limits of equitable authority and the need for structured judicial standards in contested bankruptcy remedies.

themes.name: Can bankruptcy courts override the rights of non-debtors and outsiders without their consent?
themes.definition: This question addresses the legal limits of bankruptcy jurisdiction when releases, injunctions, asset dispositions, or other remedies affect parties outside the debtor.

themes.name: Should disputed, contingent, or legally related-party obligations qualify as bankruptcy claims?
themes.definition: This question examines how the Bankruptcy Code should define claims arising from uncertain liabilities, organizational relationships, or benefits conferred through affiliated parties.

themes.name: Does collective bankruptcy fairly replace individual creditor enforcement with centralized administration?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether the collective process appropriately restrains individual remedies while coordinating claims and preserving estate value.

themes.name: Do market-oriented or private-ordering mechanisms produce more efficient and equitable restructurings than traditional Chapter 11?
themes.definition: This question compares contractual, market-based, and negotiated restructuring mechanisms with court-supervised reorganization.

themes.name: Can debt restructuring solve financial distress when the debtor’s underlying operational or economic problems remain unresolved?
themes.definition: This question distinguishes solvency relief achieved through changing financial claims from reorganization that actually restores the firm’s economic viability.

themes.name: Do Chapter 11 governance mechanisms create incentives for managers and creditors to pursue value-maximizing decisions?
themes.definition: This question examines how insolvency changes managerial duties, creditor influence, and strategic behavior before and during reorganization.

themes.name: Should financially distressed assets be sold quickly, or should bankruptcy favor a slower process that protects reorganization value and stakeholders?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the procedural and substantive safeguards governing extraordinary asset sales, transfers, or liquidation during Chapter 11.

themes.name: Are open-ended and ambiguous Bankruptcy Code provisions undermining predictable and principled bankruptcy outcomes?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether judicial interpretation of unsettled statutory language produces inconsistent results and whether clearer doctrinal standards are needed.

themes.name: Does the existing Chapter 11 framework function effectively, or is structural statutory reform or replacement necessary?
themes.definition: This question evaluates claims that Chapter 11 is dysfunctional by comparing its institutional design and outcomes with proposed amendments, specialized procedures, or market-based alternatives.

themes.name: What empirical evidence can establish whether bankruptcy courts and Chapter 11 procedures improve efficiency, fairness, and reorganization outcomes?
themes.definition: This question concerns how case outcomes, judicial practices, historical evidence, and research designs should be used to test competing claims about bankruptcy policy and institutional performance.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy distribution follow prebankruptcy contractual priorities, or should bankruptcy-specific rules override them?
themes.definition: This question examines when collective, egalitarian, or debtor-protective bankruptcy policies should displace creditors’ preexisting contractual and state-law entitlements.

themes.name: Does the absolute priority rule preserve fair value allocation between creditors and equity holders in Chapter 11?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether reorganizations should permit existing equity holders to retain value despite unpaid senior claims and whether departures from priority are justified.

themes.name: Do secured creditors’ control rights undermine Chapter 11’s ability to preserve viable businesses?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether secured-creditor remedies, objections, and bargaining power force premature liquidation or otherwise obstruct debtor rehabilitation.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy law limit quick § 363 sales and expansive security interests to protect junior and unsecured claimants?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether expedited asset sales and broad liens transfer too much going-concern value or control away from unsecured and junior stakeholders.

themes.name: How should bankruptcy allocate valuation and loss risks between secured creditors, the estate, and unsecured creditors?
themes.definition: This question concerns collateral valuation, going-concern versus liquidation value, postpetition interest, administrative expenses, and deficiencies when estate value is uncertain.

themes.name: Does debtor-in-possession financing preserve going-concern value or give new lenders excessive priority and control?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether postpetition financing enables productive reorganization or instead redistributes value from existing creditors and constrains the estate.

themes.name: Should managers’ and directors’ control and fiduciary duties change when a firm becomes insolvent or enters Chapter 11?
themes.definition: This question examines how insolvency should alter corporate governance, managerial discretion, and duties owed to creditors and the bankruptcy estate.

themes.name: Do bankruptcy procedures adequately prevent insiders, managers, and professional advisers from exploiting distressed firms?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether participants with control or informational advantages can obtain opportunistic transfers, fees, agreements, or restructuring outcomes.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy courts rely on equitable discretion or adhere more strictly to the Bankruptcy Code?
themes.definition: This question addresses the appropriate scope of judge-made doctrines, equitable powers, and policy-based interpretation when statutory commands appear incomplete or harsh.

themes.name: Can statutory interpretation provide predictable and principled answers to recurring ambiguities in the Bankruptcy Code?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether courts can reconcile conflicting provisions and poorly drafted rules without producing inconsistent, forum-dependent outcomes.

themes.name: How should bankruptcy courts resolve conflicts between federal bankruptcy rules and nonbankruptcy rights or proceedings?
themes.definition: This question concerns the interaction between bankruptcy law and state-law claims, contracts, foreclosure, regulatory processes, and other legal institutions.

themes.name: Does the automatic stay appropriately balance collective administration against creditors’ ability to enforce remedies?
themes.definition: This question examines whether restrictions on foreclosure, contract termination, and other individual enforcement actions protect reorganization without unfairly delaying or impairing creditors.

themes.name: Do Chapter 11 plan-confirmation rules adequately protect unsecured creditor classes?
themes.definition: This question evaluates voting, classification, cramdown, plan-based modification of property rights, and the treatment of unsecured claims in confirmed reorganizations.

themes.name: Does Chapter 11 bargaining improve value allocation, or does creditor factionalism turn reorganization into a contest for control?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether negotiations among creditor groups produce efficient collective solutions or strategic outcomes driven by vetoes, holdouts, and unequal leverage.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy intervene early enough to preserve viable firms, or does early intervention impose unnecessary costs and losses?
themes.definition: This question examines how the timing and duration of insolvency proceedings affect recoveries, going-concern value, and the distinction between viable and nonviable businesses.

themes.name: Is Chapter 11 economically superior to liquidation, market-based restructuring, or faster sale procedures for distressed firms?
themes.definition: This question compares court-supervised reorganization with alternative resolution mechanisms in terms of value preservation, administrative cost, speed, and stakeholder recoveries.

themes.name: Do bankruptcy courts and institutional participants possess the competence and accountability needed to manage complex reorganizations?
themes.definition: This question evaluates judicial oversight, professional influence, creditor participation, and the allocation of decision-making authority among courts, managers, creditors, and shareholders.

themes.name: Do generalized bankruptcy doctrines adequately handle complex capital structures, contingent claims, and novel financial instruments?
themes.definition: This question asks whether formal legal categories and standardized rules accurately capture the economic consequences of sophisticated transactions and claims.

themes.name: Does bankruptcy law adequately protect tort victims and other noncontractual claimants while preserving viable enterprises?
themes.definition: This question examines the distributive and institutional tension between maximizing or preserving the estate and compensating claimants whose rights were not created through ordinary contracts.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy doctrine be redesigned in light of empirical evidence about how large corporate reorganizations actually operate?
themes.definition: This question tests whether statutory assumptions and economic models fit observed practice, including outcomes of major bankruptcies and the effects of institutional or procedural reforms.

themes.name: Can Chapter 11’s collective, court-supervised process coordinate large and heterogeneous creditor claims more effectively than ordinary litigation or decentralized enforcement?
themes.definition: This question examines whether bankruptcy’s collective procedures can resolve complex, conflicting claims while reducing individual creditor races and duplicative litigation.

themes.name: Does Chapter 11 preserve going-concern value, or does contemporary practice increasingly favor liquidation, asset sales, and financially driven exits?
themes.definition: This question compares traditional plan-based rehabilitation with expedited sales and other mechanisms that may transfer or liquidate the business rather than reorganize it.

themes.name: When should control of a distressed company shift from incumbent management and shareholders to creditors or external oversight?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the legal and economic triggers for reallocating corporate decision-making authority during financial distress and Chapter 11.

themes.name: Does the absolute priority rule adequately protect creditor priority while allowing feasible and value-maximizing reorganizations?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether deviations from priority, including residual equity participation, are necessary or unfairly transfer value from senior claimants.

themes.name: Should secured creditors’ priority extend beyond identified collateral to a debtor’s going-concern or enterprise value?
themes.definition: This question addresses how bankruptcy should divide appreciation, reorganization value, and overencumbered collateral between secured lenders and other claimants.

themes.name: Does Chapter 11 unfairly transfer value from unsecured, junior, or nonconsensual claimants to secured and financial creditors?
themes.definition: This question examines whether financing arrangements, valuation practices, and restructuring devices systematically favor senior financial claims over other stakeholders.

themes.name: How should bankruptcy distribute limited estate value between creditor recoveries and reorganization expenses, professional fees, and other administrative payments?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether payments made to professionals and other postpetition interests are justified by the value they provide to the estate.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy law permit favored or exceptional treatment for individual creditors when that treatment conflicts with collective creditor equality?
themes.definition: This question evaluates preferences, special settlements, roll-ups, and other arrangements that give particular creditors advantages outside ordinary distribution priorities.

themes.name: Do prepetition contracts and private creditor arrangements deserve enforcement after filing, or should Chapter 11 override them to serve collective reorganization goals?
themes.definition: This question examines the enforceability of prebankruptcy bargains, intercreditor agreements, and private remedies once a bankruptcy case begins.

themes.name: Does the Bankruptcy Code provide a coherent framework for assumption, assignment, and rejection of executory contracts in a restructuring?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how contract treatment affects value, counterparties’ rights, and the debtor’s ability to reorganize.

themes.name: Should Chapter 11 governance and procedural rules be tailored to materially different debtor sizes, industries, and case complexities?
themes.definition: This question challenges whether a largely uniform process appropriately handles heterogeneous corporate bankruptcies or instead creates avoidable costs and distortions.

themes.name: Does greater judicial discretion improve equitable and efficient bankruptcy outcomes, or does it create unacceptable uncertainty and litigation costs?
themes.definition: This question assesses the proper scope of courts’ discretionary authority in applying flexible, policy-based, or exceptional bankruptcy remedies.

themes.name: How should courts resolve conflicts between strict Bankruptcy Code text, prebankruptcy legal rights, and bankruptcy’s substantive policy goals?
themes.definition: This question addresses statutory interpretation when formal rules conflict with reorganization, fairness, value-maximization, or debtor-protection objectives.

themes.name: Are bankruptcy courts institutionally capable of supervising complex reorganizations and resolving disputes involving nonbankruptcy rights and governmental authority?
themes.definition: This question examines the jurisdictional, constitutional, and practical limits of bankruptcy courts in coordinating financially and legally complex cases.

themes.name: Can bankruptcy procedures effectively constrain strategic, coercive, or opportunistic behavior by debtors, creditors, managers, and other stakeholders?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether voting, disclosure, financing, plan, and court-approval mechanisms prevent individual actors from undermining collective outcomes.

themes.name: Does incumbent debtor management create agency costs that harm creditors, and do oversight, compensation controls, or external management improve reorganization results?
themes.definition: This question focuses on managerial incentives, executive bonuses, and the institutional mechanisms used to align management with the estate and its claimants.

themes.name: Can market-based valuation, creditor bargaining, and private consent reliably produce fair and efficient Chapter 11 outcomes?
themes.definition: This question tests whether market mechanisms and negotiated resolutions accurately value distressed firms and legitimately allocate control and recoveries.

themes.name: Should financially distressed firms resolve their problems through out-of-court workouts and private contracting rather than court-supervised Chapter 11 proceedings?
themes.definition: This question compares the flexibility and speed of private restructuring with bankruptcy’s collective protections, binding effects, and dispute-resolution capacity.

themes.name: Should Chapter 11 plans or bankruptcy orders bind non-debtor parties that have not themselves filed for bankruptcy?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the legitimacy and legal limits of third-party releases, non-debtor protections, and other extensions of bankruptcy effects.

themes.name: Does Chapter 11 adequately accommodate shareholders, tort claimants, employees, regulators, and other non-financial stakeholders while preserving enterprise value?
themes.definition: This question examines whether the process balances creditor recovery and reorganization against the rights of parties whose interests are not captured by ordinary debt priorities.

themes.name: When should Chapter 11 preserve a viable business as a going concern rather than facilitate liquidation?
themes.definition: This question examines how enterprise viability, creditor recoveries, transaction costs, and broader social value should determine whether a distressed firm is reorganized or liquidated.

themes.name: Do whole-business § 363 sales create more value than traditional Chapter 11 reorganizations?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether expedited asset sales maximize value and creditor recoveries or instead bypass procedural safeguards and undermine collective reorganization.

themes.name: Does the absolute priority rule appropriately determine whether equityholders may retain value in Chapter 11?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether deviations from priority are justified by valuation uncertainty, bargaining needs, or reorganization objectives.

themes.name: Does secured-creditor control improve Chapter 11 outcomes or extract value from junior stakeholders?
themes.definition: This question examines how liens, credit agreements, distressed-debt acquisitions, and lender influence affect reorganization efficiency and distributions.

themes.name: Do debtor-in-possession managers create excessive agency costs and moral hazard during reorganization?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether managers controlling the debtor remain properly incentivized or require stronger creditor and court monitoring.

themes.name: Who should control corporate decision-making during Chapter 11: managers, creditors, equityholders, or the court?
themes.definition: This question analyzes how procedural control should be allocated among competing constituencies to preserve firm value while limiting opportunism.

themes.name: Does Chapter 11 adequately balance debtor flexibility against creditor protection?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether the debtor receives enough operational and bargaining freedom without impairing creditor monitoring, participation, or recovery.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy law permit unequal treatment of creditors to advance reorganization or other distributional goals?
themes.definition: This question examines when departures from formal equality and neutral treatment are legally or economically defensible.

themes.name: How far should federal bankruptcy law alter preexisting state-law contractual, property, and creditor rights?
themes.definition: This question addresses the extent to which bankruptcy can modify, extinguish, or subordinate rights created outside bankruptcy.

themes.name: Can ex ante contracts legitimately determine bankruptcy control and distribution when they bind parties during financial distress?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether private agreements should displace bankruptcy defaults and whether distressed-party consent is genuinely voluntary.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy courts use broad discretion or clearer rules when interpreting ambiguous Chapter 11 provisions?
themes.definition: This question compares flexible, purposive adjudication with formal, predictable statutory interpretation in resolving gaps and conflicts in bankruptcy doctrine.

themes.name: Can collective restructuring fairly bind nonconsenting or absent creditors?
themes.definition: This question examines the justification and limits of replacing individual collection rights with procedures that coordinate dispersed claims and impose outcomes on dissenters.

themes.name: How should valuation uncertainty affect the allowance, classification, and distribution of creditor claims?
themes.definition: This question studies whether existing valuation methods and procedural rules reliably determine recoveries, deficiency claims, and enterprise value.

themes.name: Do bankruptcy professionals’ compensation and conflicts distort Chapter 11 outcomes?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether attorneys, financial advisers, and other professionals are sufficiently independent and properly incentivized when their fees are paid from the estate.

themes.name: Are bankruptcy courts institutionally equipped to supervise complex large-corporate reorganizations?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether court expertise, staffing, case allocation, factual review, and professional oversight adequately support large Chapter 11 cases.

themes.name: Does competition among bankruptcy venues or insolvency regimes improve corporate-bankruptcy outcomes?
themes.definition: This question examines whether venue choice and jurisdictional competition produce efficient and legitimate reorganizations or enable strategic forum shopping.

themes.name: Do Chapter 11’s procedures achieve genuine reorganization rather than wealth redistribution among stakeholders?
themes.definition: This question tests whether the system preserves productive firms and creates value or primarily reallocates existing value through bargaining and procedural leverage.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy law accommodate employees, communities, governments, and other noncreditor stakeholders?
themes.definition: This question examines whether creditor recovery should remain the dominant objective when reorganization decisions impose significant external costs on connected parties.

themes.name: Are avoidance and estate-augmentation powers appropriately used to recover transfers benefiting selected creditors?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the scope of trustee authority to unwind secured or preferential transactions and enhance collective recoveries.

themes.name: Does empirical evidence support major statutory reform of Chapter 11?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether caseload data, case outcomes, market behavior, and quantitative models substantiate claims that Chapter 11 is inefficient, unfair, or obsolete.

themes.name: Does collective bankruptcy enforcement produce greater value than allowing individual creditors to pursue separate remedies?
themes.definition: This question examines whether the automatic stay, centralized administration, and collective distribution of bankruptcy better protect total creditor value than decentralized collection, foreclosure, or private contracting.

themes.name: Should Chapter 11 favor preserving a distressed firm's going-concern value over liquidating its assets?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how asset valuation, business configuration, market-tested sales, and judicial valuation should determine whether reorganization or liquidation yields the superior outcome.

themes.name: Should control of a Chapter 11 debtor remain with the debtor in possession or shift to creditors and other bankruptcy actors?
themes.definition: This question addresses how decision-making authority should be divided among incumbent managers, creditors, trustees, examiners, and courts during reorganization.

themes.name: Do Chapter 11 governance rules adequately control conflicts among managers, shareholders, and creditors?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether insolvency-specific duties, voting rights, and judicial oversight align managerial and equity-holder incentives with maximizing firm value and protecting creditors.

themes.name: How far may bankruptcy law limit or alter the rights and remedies of secured creditors?
themes.definition: This question concerns the permissible scope of stays, valuation rules, lien priorities, plan confirmation, and other bankruptcy interventions affecting secured lenders.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy priority rules preserve prebankruptcy entitlements or permit unequal distributions to advance restructuring objectives?
themes.definition: This question evaluates when deviations from priority, pro rata equality, or prepetition contractual rankings are justified among secured, unsecured, senior, junior, and residual claimants.

themes.name: Does bankruptcy law properly reconcile federal bankruptcy policy with state-law property and contract rights?
themes.definition: This question examines the extent to which bankruptcy should respect rights created outside the proceeding under principles such as Butner while still implementing federal restructuring policies.

themes.name: Can avoidance and preference rules fairly recover value without destabilizing otherwise valid commercial transactions?
themes.definition: This question studies when bankruptcy law should invalidate, recharacterize, or recover prepetition transfers that were enforceable under ordinary nonbankruptcy law.

themes.name: Do the automatic stay and related Chapter 11 protections provide necessary breathing space or enable strategic delay and opportunism?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether debtor-protective stays and procedural protections preserve reorganizable businesses or instead encourage delay, coercion, or opportunistic filings.

themes.name: Do collective voting, cramdown, and consent mechanisms effectively overcome holdouts and free riding in debt restructurings?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether Chapter 11 bargaining and voting procedures enable value-preserving restructurings without improperly coercing dissenting creditors.

themes.name: Do creditor-driven transactions and distressed-debt strategies reallocate value in ways that harm the debtor or other creditor classes?
themes.definition: This question examines how credit trading, strategic litigation, credit bidding, and other creditor self-protection mechanisms affect collective recoveries and restructuring outcomes.

themes.name: Should corporate bankruptcy give greater weight to employees, tort victims, communities, and other noncreditor stakeholders?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether creditor recovery and value maximization should be constrained by harms imposed on constituencies affected by the debtor’s financial distress.

themes.name: Are ordinary bankruptcy rules adequate for mass-tort, contingent, future, and otherwise atypical claims?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether claim estimation, classification, priority, discharge, and distribution mechanisms fairly administer uncertain or nontraditional liabilities.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy courts resolve ambiguous statutory questions through categorical rules or flexible, context-sensitive standards?
themes.definition: This question compares predictable textual or rule-based approaches with multi-factor, policy-based, and discretionary interpretation of unsettled Bankruptcy Code provisions.

themes.name: What are the legitimate limits of bankruptcy-court authority over nondebtor parties, assets, and transactions?
themes.definition: This question examines when courts may scrutinize, authorize, enjoin, or bind conduct beyond the debtor and estate through extraordinary bankruptcy powers.

themes.name: Do Chapter 11’s costs, delays, and adversarial procedures undermine its ability to reorganize viable businesses?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether administrative expense, litigation, procedural complexity, and court involvement make Chapter 11 too slow or costly relative to its restructuring benefits.

themes.name: Does the institutional design of Chapter 11 provide credible representation and legitimate decision-making for competing stakeholders?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the roles of bankruptcy judges, professionals, committees, independent actors, and procedural safeguards in producing fair and trusted reorganizations.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy policy maximize creditor value or pursue broader organizational and social objectives?
themes.definition: This question addresses the normative foundation of corporate bankruptcy and whether creditor recovery should prevail over preservation of firms, employment, markets, or other stakeholder interests.

themes.name: Are Chapter 11 asset sales and structured dismissals legitimate substitutes for a traditional plan of reorganization?
themes.definition: This question examines whether nontraditional case-ending mechanisms can efficiently resolve distress without evading priority rules, creditor voting, or statutory protections.

themes.name: Do existing insolvency institutions adequately handle large, complex, and systemically important corporate failures?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether current bankruptcy rules, courts, and restructuring mechanisms remain workable for complex capital structures, interconnected firms, and modern lending practices.

themes.name: Should financially distressed firms be reorganized as going concerns rather than liquidated?
themes.definition: This question examines whether bankruptcy law can reliably distinguish economically viable businesses worth preserving from firms whose continuation destroys value.

themes.name: Does Chapter 11 preserve going-concern value while producing efficient creditor recoveries?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether Chapter 11’s institutional design actually improves value and recoveries compared with liquidation, private workouts, or other restructuring mechanisms.

themes.name: How should individual creditor enforcement rights be constrained within a collective bankruptcy process?
themes.definition: This question addresses when bankruptcy’s centralized administration should displace separate creditor remedies in order to prevent a destructive race for assets.

themes.name: When may bankruptcy law depart from creditor priority and other prebankruptcy entitlements?
themes.definition: This question examines whether equitable or reorganization-based objectives justify altering statutory priorities, contractual rights, or ordinary property rules.

themes.name: Does secured-creditor control improve or undermine Chapter 11 reorganizations?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how liens, seniority, and secured-creditor influence affect bargaining power, case administration, and outcomes for junior creditors and the debtor.

themes.name: How should corporate control be allocated among managers, shareholders, and creditors during financial distress?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether control should remain with debtor management or shift toward creditors as insolvency changes the distribution of economic risk.

themes.name: Are managerial agency problems in debtor-in-possession reorganizations adequately controlled?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether managers can favor themselves or particular investor classes and whether fiduciary duties, court oversight, and other safeguards prevent such conduct.

themes.name: How much discretion should bankruptcy courts have to achieve equitable results?
themes.definition: This question tests the proper boundary between judicial flexibility in unusual cases and adherence to statutory text, creditor priority, and predictable rules.

themes.name: How should courts interpret ambiguous or incomplete Bankruptcy Code provisions?
themes.definition: This question examines the relative authority of statutory text, pre-Code doctrine, state-law rights, legislative history, equitable principles, and legislative purpose in bankruptcy interpretation.

themes.name: Does legal uncertainty and procedural complexity generate inefficient strategic behavior in bankruptcy?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether unclear doctrine, costly litigation, and burdensome procedures encourage delay, forum shopping, holdouts, or other value-reducing tactics.

themes.name: Should private contracting determine creditor entitlements, or should mandatory bankruptcy rules prevail?
themes.definition: This question addresses the appropriate division between prebankruptcy contractual arrangements and public, court-supervised rules governing collective insolvency.

themes.name: Do bankruptcy rules create appropriate incentives for lending and investment before financial distress?
themes.definition: This question studies whether collection rights, priority rules, enforcement protections, and expected bankruptcy outcomes improve or distort ex ante financing behavior.

themes.name: How should information and valuation shape creditor participation and distributions in Chapter 11?
themes.definition: This question examines whether disclosure, valuation methods, and participation rights enable courts and creditors to allocate control, claims, and recoveries accurately.

themes.name: Can expedited asset sales provide a better alternative to traditional Chapter 11 reorganization?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether court-supervised collateral or business sales preserve value and protect stakeholders better than a negotiated plan process.

themes.name: Do preference-avoidance rules promote equal distribution without imposing excessive uncertainty and administrative costs?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether rules requiring creditors to return prepetition payments fairly reduce preferential recoveries while remaining coherent and administrable.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy law make creditor-initiated or involuntary cases easier to commence?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether the benefits of early creditor intervention outweigh the risks of strategic filings, harassment, and premature loss of debtor control.

themes.name: Should employee wage claims receive priority over secured and other creditor claims?
themes.definition: This question examines whether employee-protective distribution rules are justified by fairness and social policy despite their effects on lending, recoveries, and reorganization costs.

themes.name: Can bankruptcy courts effectively administer complex liabilities and large-scale Chapter 11 cases?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether courts possess the institutional capacity, procedures, and oversight mechanisms needed for mega-cases and unusually complex creditor structures.

themes.name: Should Chapter 11 provide different procedures for small businesses and cases of differing complexity?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether simplified or specialized bankruptcy procedures improve small-business outcomes without sacrificing creditor protection and accountability.

themes.name: When should bankruptcy proceedings protect nondebtor parties from liability or enforcement?
themes.definition: This question addresses the legal and institutional limits of extending bankruptcy-related protections, releases, or remedies to parties that have not themselves entered bankruptcy.

themes.name: Does Chapter 11 preserve viable enterprises, or mainly delay liquidation?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether reorganization proceedings successfully identify and preserve going-concern value rather than prolonging the failure of firms that should be liquidated.

themes.name: How should control be allocated between a debtor in possession and its creditors during reorganization?
themes.definition: This question examines when incumbent managers should retain decision-making authority and when creditors or other institutions should obtain greater control over the distressed firm.

themes.name: Do Chapter 11 governance rules adequately constrain managerial and controlling-shareholder self-interest?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether bankruptcy governance aligns managers’ and controllers’ incentives with enterprise value and the interests of creditors and other constituencies.

themes.name: How should bankruptcy reconcile creditor equality with secured-creditor priority?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether preferential treatment of secured claims is justified and how it affects unsecured recoveries, distributions, and incentives to maximize estate value.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy give creditors rights beyond those available under nonbankruptcy law?
themes.definition: This question examines the proper scope of bankruptcy-created protections, remedies, and priorities relative to prepetition contractual and state-law entitlements.

themes.name: When may bankruptcy law override or modify prebankruptcy property and contractual rights?
themes.definition: This question addresses the limits of federal bankruptcy authority to alter privately arranged rights while preserving the state-law baseline reflected in doctrines such as Butner.

themes.name: Can dissenting or nonparticipating creditors legitimately be bound by a reorganization plan?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the justification and procedural safeguards for imposing plan treatment on creditors who do not consent, participate, or challenge the debtor’s proposal.

themes.name: How much judicial discretion should bankruptcy courts exercise when statutory rules are ambiguous or produce inequitable outcomes?
themes.definition: This question concerns the proper balance between statutory fidelity, predictable rules, and flexible judicial intervention in difficult Chapter 11 cases.

themes.name: What is the proper jurisdictional and institutional role of the bankruptcy court in complex Chapter 11 cases?
themes.definition: This question examines how far bankruptcy courts should reach into disputes, transactions, and governance matters affecting the estate and creditor distributions.

themes.name: How should courts allocate valuation and timing risks when the worth of assets or claims is uncertain?
themes.definition: This question addresses judicial methods for valuing intangible, contingent, or disputed interests and determining which constituencies should bear the resulting uncertainty.

themes.name: Do creditor-participation, disclosure, and voting rules adequately protect less powerful or absent claimants?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether Chapter 11 procedures provide meaningful information, monitoring opportunities, representation, and protection for creditors unable to negotiate directly.

themes.name: Does the automatic stay appropriately balance collective administration against creditors’ enforcement rights?
themes.definition: This question examines when bankruptcy should suspend individual collection and litigation efforts and when creditors should be permitted to proceed against the debtor or its assets.

themes.name: To what extent should bankruptcy permit rejection or modification of ongoing contractual relationships?
themes.definition: This question concerns the treatment of executory contracts and other continuing obligations when enforcing them may either preserve or destroy reorganization value.

themes.name: Can debt-to-equity conversion improve reorganized-firm viability without unfairly reallocating stakeholder value?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether converting debt claims into equity is an effective alternative to liquidation and how it affects capital structure, control, and creditor recoveries.

themes.name: Are uniform Chapter 11 rules appropriate for heterogeneous firms and creditor relationships?
themes.definition: This question tests whether a one-size-fits-all reorganization regime adequately accommodates differences in business type, financial structure, claim complexity, and distress conditions.

themes.name: Do the costs and delays of formal bankruptcy outweigh its value as a collective resolution mechanism?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether procedural complexity, transaction costs, delay, and litigation liabilities undermine the benefits of centralized business reorganization.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy protect non-debtor, community, or other broader stakeholder interests in addition to creditors and owners?
themes.definition: This question examines whether reorganization law should redistribute protection toward employees, communities, nonconsensual claimants, or other stakeholders affected by corporate distress.

themes.name: Should avoidance and preference rules invalidate transactions that reduce creditor recoveries without producing a genuine estate benefit?
themes.definition: This question evaluates when bankruptcy should unwind transfers, charges, or security interests that are formally valid under state law but allegedly diminish collective recoveries.

themes.name: Can private ordering or state-law alternatives perform bankruptcy’s functions more effectively?
themes.definition: This question compares formal federal bankruptcy with contractual workouts, market-based arrangements, and state-law debt-enforcement or restructuring mechanisms.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy prioritize efficiency and enterprise-value preservation over strict enforcement of prebankruptcy entitlements?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether bankruptcy’s central objective should be economically efficient reorganization or faithful preservation of preexisting rights and creditor bargains.

themes.name: To what extent may bankruptcy law alter creditors’ prebankruptcy state-law and contractual rights?
themes.definition: This question examines the federal bankruptcy power to modify, preserve, or override property, contract, and creditor-remedy rights created outside bankruptcy.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy’s collective process override privately negotiated creditor priorities and decentralized enforcement?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether collective bankruptcy administration produces better coordination and distributions than private contracting and individual creditor recovery.

themes.name: Do the cost and procedural burdens of traditional Chapter 11 prevent viable businesses from reorganizing?
themes.definition: This question tests whether expense, delay, and procedural complexity cause financially viable firms to liquidate or abandon reorganization unnecessarily.

themes.name: Should Chapter 11 favor reorganizing distressed firms or liquidating enterprises that cannot create going-concern value?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether reorganization law can reliably distinguish businesses worth preserving from those whose assets should be liquidated.

themes.name: How should control of a Chapter 11 case be divided between debtor management, secured creditors, unsecured creditors, and equity holders?
themes.definition: This question addresses how voting, financing, governance, and court-supervision rules allocate reorganization power among competing constituencies.

themes.name: Do secured lending and DIP-financing arrangements give senior creditors excessive control over the debtor’s reorganization?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether collateral rights, lender influence, and postpetition financing terms constrain the debtor and subordinate other stakeholders excessively.

themes.name: Should the absolute priority rule preserve prebankruptcy priorities or permit deviations to facilitate consensual and value-maximizing reorganizations?
themes.definition: This question examines when bankruptcy may redistribute value across creditor classes and equity despite the parties’ prepetition priority arrangements.

themes.name: How should bankruptcy protect unsecured creditors from value diversion by secured or otherwise favored claimants?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether bankruptcy rules adequately prevent estate value from being transferred to particular creditors at the expense of the general creditor body.

themes.name: When should courts grant relief from the automatic stay to protect a creditor’s nonbankruptcy rights?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how courts should balance individual enforcement of collateral or other rights against preserving the collective reorganization process.

themes.name: To what extent may a debtor reject, modify, or continue ongoing contracts over the counterparty’s objection?
themes.definition: This question addresses how Chapter 11 should balance the debtor’s need to restructure contractual obligations against counterparties’ ordinary contract rights.

themes.name: Are existing Chapter 11 doctrines adequate for reorganizing mass-tort and other liabilities involving claimants beyond the debtor’s estate?
themes.definition: This question tests whether ordinary bankruptcy categories and procedures can fairly and lawfully resolve dispersed, contingent, or nondebtor-related claims.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy courts use broad equitable powers to alter rights beyond the debtor’s estate?
themes.definition: This question examines the legitimacy and limits of injunctions, third-party protections, and other extraordinary remedies affecting nondebtors.

themes.name: How should courts interpret ambiguous Bankruptcy Code provisions when statutory text conflicts with precedent, pre-Code doctrine, or bankruptcy policy?
themes.definition: This question concerns the appropriate interpretive method for resolving uncertainty and disagreement in the statutory framework governing insolvency.

themes.name: Do context-sensitive judicial standards produce better bankruptcy outcomes than categorical statutory rules?
themes.definition: This question compares flexible, fact-specific adjudication with bright-line rules in terms of predictability, fairness, and economic consequences.

themes.name: How should valuation uncertainty affect plan confirmation and the allocation of enterprise value among creditor classes?
themes.definition: This question addresses the evidentiary and legal standards courts should use when disputed valuations determine priority, impairment, or distributions.

themes.name: How should bankruptcy law address holdouts and collective-action problems among bondholders and junior creditors?
themes.definition: This question evaluates contractual and procedural mechanisms for preventing individual creditors from blocking or extracting value from a restructuring.

themes.name: Do creditor classification, representation, and voting rules give all materially affected parties legitimate influence over a restructuring?
themes.definition: This question examines whether Chapter 11 participation structures accurately represent divergent creditor interests and prevent strategic manipulation of voting outcomes.

themes.name: Should Chapter 11 favor rapid asset sales and financing or require a fuller plan-based reorganization?
themes.definition: This question compares speed-oriented value preservation with the disclosure, bargaining, and procedural protections associated with traditional reorganization.

themes.name: How should bankruptcy rules control managerial, shareholder, and creditor incentives during impending corporate failure?
themes.definition: This question concerns agency conflicts and the design of legal and financial rules that discourage opportunism while preserving incentives to maximize enterprise value.

themes.name: How should bankruptcy treat complex financing structures and floating security interests whose legal and economic effects were not clearly anticipated?
themes.definition: This question examines whether existing priority and enforcement rules can fairly resolve disputes created by novel capital structures, collateral arrangements, and prepetition transactions.

themes.name: When may bankruptcy law alter or extinguish prebankruptcy contractual and property rights?
themes.definition: This question examines whether bankruptcy courts and statutes may reallocate, suspend, or eliminate rights that would remain enforceable under nonbankruptcy law in order to facilitate reorganization.

themes.name: How far should Chapter 11 be permitted to modify secured creditors’ rights?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the legal limits on impairing collateral, payment rights, enforcement remedies, or priority protections held by secured creditors during reorganization.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy depart from equality and absolute priority to redistribute value among stakeholders?
themes.definition: This question asks when, if ever, bankruptcy distribution rules should favor particular constituencies or permit junior interests to recover before senior claims are fully satisfied.

themes.name: Who should control major decisions in a large-company Chapter 11 case?
themes.definition: This question investigates how governance power should be divided among incumbent management, the debtor, secured lenders, unsecured creditors, equity holders, professionals, and the court.

themes.name: Do Chapter 11 procedures adequately protect junior, unsecured, dispersed, and otherwise weak creditors?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether voting rules, representation, disclosure, oversight, and distribution mechanisms prevent powerful participants from diverting value from less powerful claimants.

themes.name: Can private bargaining and market mechanisms solve creditor-coordination problems better than collective bankruptcy procedures?
themes.definition: This question compares contractual, negotiated, and market-based restructuring with centralized judicial or statutory intervention in resolving collective-action problems.

themes.name: When should preserving a distressed firm as a going concern take priority over liquidation?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether reorganization creates more aggregate value than state-law liquidation while accounting for creditor recoveries, delay, and the costs of preserving the business.

themes.name: Do expedited section 363 sales sacrifice creditor protections for speed and value maximization?
themes.definition: This question examines whether distressed-asset sales outside the ordinary plan process improperly bypass disclosure, bidding, voting, and other Chapter 11 safeguards.

themes.name: Do Chapter 11 voting and confirmation rules legitimately bind claimants who did not consent to the plan?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether class voting, cramdown, plan classification, and participation requirements fairly authorize a reorganization’s treatment of dissenting or absent creditors.

themes.name: Do DIP financing arrangements improperly concentrate control and value in senior lenders?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether debtor-in-possession financing, liens, milestones, and related court orders protect the estate or enable dominant financiers to control or terminate the reorganization.

themes.name: How should ambiguous Bankruptcy Code provisions be interpreted in novel and fact-intensive disputes?
themes.definition: This question compares textual, purposive, structural, historical, and equitable methods for resolving bankruptcy issues that the statutory language does not clearly answer.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy judges use broad equitable discretion or predictable categorical rules?
themes.definition: This question asks whether fact-sensitive judicial judgment improves fairness and functionality or instead creates uncertainty, inconsistent outcomes, and higher restructuring costs.

themes.name: Does the Bankruptcy Code adequately govern complex corporate reorganizations in practice?
themes.definition: This question tests whether statutory rules and institutional design provide coherent, workable standards for modern business cases or leave a damaging gap between formal doctrine and actual practice.

themes.name: How should Chapter 11 balance debtor rehabilitation against the interests of nondebtor stakeholders?
themes.definition: This question examines the treatment of workers, retirees, counterparties, public institutions, and other parties whose interests are affected by restructuring but who are not the debtor.

themes.name: What limits should govern a trustee or estate representative’s authority to pursue claims against creditors and third parties?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the scope of estate representatives’ discretion to control, transfer, release, or litigate claims involving assets and obligations connected to the bankruptcy estate.

themes.name: Do professional fees, litigation, and administrative procedures consume too much of the bankruptcy estate?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether advisers, lawyers, valuation disputes, and procedural requirements reduce creditor recoveries enough to undermine bankruptcy’s substantive objectives.

themes.name: Is Chapter 11 suitably designed for small-business bankruptcies?
themes.definition: This question compares the costs, procedural demands, creditor protections, and rehabilitation benefits of Chapter 11 in small cases with those in large corporate reorganizations.

themes.name: Can Chapter 11 provide a comprehensive and binding resolution for mass-tort liabilities?
themes.definition: This question examines whether reorganization can fairly aggregate, value, represent, and permanently resolve claims held by large groups of present and future tort claimants.

themes.name: Do financial-engineering and distressed-debt transactions solve financial distress or merely redistribute and obscure its consequences?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether complex financing, claim-trading, and restructuring techniques create genuine enterprise value or primarily rearrange bargaining power and losses.

themes.name: Does Chapter 11 actually preserve going-concern value and maximize creditor recoveries at acceptable cost?
themes.definition: This question uses functional and empirical evidence to test whether business bankruptcy achieves its stated value-preservation objectives better than liquidation or alternative restructuring mechanisms.

themes.name: Does Chapter 11 maximize the value of the operating firm more effectively than liquidation or creditor-by-creditor enforcement?
themes.definition: This question examines whether court-supervised reorganization preserves greater going-concern value and produces better overall outcomes than liquidation or decentralized collection.

themes.name: How should Chapter 11 balance creditor recovery against the preservation of a distressed firm as a going concern?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether bankruptcy law should prioritize repayment of creditors or rehabilitation of the debtor when those objectives conflict.

themes.name: Should secured creditors’ foreclosure and priority rights prevail over collective reorganization objectives?
themes.definition: This question concerns when bankruptcy should preserve, restrict, or subordinate secured lenders’ prepetition rights to protect the estate and other stakeholders.

themes.name: Do bankruptcy priority rules allocate value fairly between secured, unsecured, senior, and junior creditors?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether formal priority structures appropriately determine recoveries when the estate cannot satisfy all claims.

themes.name: How should control shift among management, shareholders, and creditors during Chapter 11?
themes.definition: This question analyzes whether decision-making authority should remain with incumbent managers and equity holders or move toward creditors as insolvency deepens.

themes.name: Can shareholders retain equity through new value without violating the absolute-priority rule?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether prepetition shareholders may receive or retain ownership in a reorganized firm when senior creditors are not paid in full.

themes.name: Does the collective bankruptcy process protect creditors better than individual enforcement outside bankruptcy?
themes.definition: This question compares bankruptcy’s coordinated distribution and asset-preservation mechanisms with fragmented creditor collection and class-based enforcement.

themes.name: Do the automatic stay and related Chapter 11 protections provide useful breathing space or mainly enable strategic delay?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether restrictions on creditor remedies facilitate productive reorganization or allow debtors to postpone inevitable liquidation and creditor recovery.

themes.name: How do creditor coordination, holdouts, and representation affect Chapter 11 outcomes?
themes.definition: This question examines whether fragmented or strategically organized creditors improve bargaining and recoveries or obstruct efficient reorganization.

themes.name: Should Chapter 11 permit debtors to modify contracts, claims, or obligations involving nondebtor parties?
themes.definition: This question concerns the permissible scope of restructuring powers over ongoing contractual relationships and liabilities owed to parties outside the bankruptcy estate.

themes.name: How should bankruptcy reconcile prepetition contractual and state-law rights with federal collective bankruptcy objectives?
themes.definition: This question investigates when the Bankruptcy Code should preserve, displace, or alter rights created before filing under contract or nonbankruptcy law.

themes.name: Does formal legal classification accurately reflect the economic substance of bankruptcy claims and transactions?
themes.definition: This question asks whether labels such as debt, equity, secured claim, or unsecured claim produce appropriate outcomes when the underlying economic arrangement is more complex.

themes.name: How should bankruptcy law treat complex financing structures that create uncertainty about priority, control, or recovery?
themes.definition: This question examines whether existing rules adequately govern novel credit instruments, contractual arrangements, and transactions involving distressed firms.

themes.name: When should courts use equitable powers to prevent transactions or plans that undermine creditor protections?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the legitimacy and limits of judicial discretion to restrict formally permissible arrangements that produce inequitable or strategically abusive results.

themes.name: Should ambiguous Bankruptcy Code provisions be resolved through judicial discretion or more determinate statutory rules?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether courts should develop context-sensitive interpretations or whether legislative clarification and tighter doctrinal standards are preferable.

themes.name: How much judicial oversight should apply to managerial decisions, extraordinary asset dispositions, and professional conduct in Chapter 11?
themes.definition: This question examines whether bankruptcy courts adequately supervise debtor management, major transactions, fees, and case administration without imposing excessive delay or cost.

themes.name: Do conflicts of interest and fiduciary failures distort valuation, restructuring decisions, and distributions in bankruptcy?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether insiders, trustees, professionals, or other controlling actors make decisions that favor particular constituencies over the estate as a whole.

themes.name: Do Chapter 11 plan-confirmation rules fairly regulate treatment of nonconsenting creditors and other stakeholders?
themes.definition: This question concerns the legitimacy of confirming plans that bind dissenting parties or affect their claims, rights, and recoveries without their agreement.

themes.name: How do bankruptcy procedure and institutional design affect delay, professional costs, creditor participation, and recoveries?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether the structure and administration of Chapter 11 cases produce efficient and accurate decisions or impose avoidable costs on creditors and debtors.

themes.name: Should Chapter 11 be replaced or supplemented by market-oriented or less judicially supervised restructuring mechanisms?
themes.definition: This question compares court-centered reorganization with private ordering, alternative dispute resolution, and other institutional reforms as means of resolving corporate distress.

themes.name: Should Chapter 11 give creditors greater control over a distressed firm's decisions, or preserve managerial and debtor autonomy?
themes.definition: This question examines how control over operations, financing, and reorganization should be divided between incumbent managers, creditors, shareholders, and new owners.

themes.name: Does prioritizing reorganization of viable businesses over liquidation preserve more value than creditor-driven enforcement?
themes.definition: This question evaluates when Chapter 11 should protect a going concern from liquidation and when liquidation is the more efficient resolution.

themes.name: Do secured-creditor priority and blanket liens promote efficient lending and resolution, or enable opportunistic control of distressed firms?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether secured lending arrangements preserve enterprise value or allow lenders to extract private benefits at the expense of junior creditors and the business.

themes.name: How should bankruptcy distribute limited value among secured creditors, unsecured creditors, equity holders, and other competing claimants?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether formal priority rules, equal treatment principles, or broader distributional considerations should determine recoveries when assets are insufficient.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy recognize and protect future, contingent, unknown, or non-debtor stakeholder claims in the same way as existing creditor claims?
themes.definition: This question examines how insolvency proceedings should represent claimants whose injuries, obligations, or interests are not fully known at the petition date.

themes.name: When should bankruptcy override prebankruptcy contracts and legal entitlements to preserve collective value?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether and under what bankruptcy-based justification valid contractual, property, or creditor rights should be modified in reorganization.

themes.name: Does centralized bankruptcy administration produce fairer and more efficient outcomes than allowing individual creditors to pursue separate remedies?
themes.definition: This question compares collective claim administration and centralized control with fragmented enforcement, creditor exit, and individual collection actions.

themes.name: Do creditor voting, classification, and majority-rule mechanisms fairly resolve conflicts among creditor groups in Chapter 11 plans?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether voting thresholds and class structures accurately translate creditor entitlements into legitimate control over plan approval.

themes.name: Do bankruptcy sales and restructuring plans preserve going-concern value for junior creditors, or transfer it to controlling parties?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether asset sales and plan transactions fairly capture enterprise value or permit senior or dominant constituencies to appropriate value.

themes.name: How far may bankruptcy courts use equitable powers or federal common law beyond the Bankruptcy Code's express text?
themes.definition: This question addresses the constitutional, statutory, and doctrinal limits on judicially created remedies and principles in bankruptcy proceedings.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy judges resolve statutory uncertainty through flexible policy-based discretion or through predictable rule-bound interpretation?
themes.definition: This question examines the proper balance between judicial adaptability, textual fidelity, precedent, legal history, and consistency in bankruptcy decisions.

themes.name: How should federal bankruptcy law interact with state property, corporate, regulatory, and commercial law?
themes.definition: This question evaluates when federal bankruptcy rules should displace, preserve, or incorporate nonbankruptcy legal rules that define rights in the estate.

themes.name: Do professional fees, litigation, and estate-funded decision-making undermine the efficiency and accountability of Chapter 11?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether lawyers, financial advisers, and other professionals create agency costs or value-enhancing oversight when paid from estate or creditor resources.

themes.name: Can judicial oversight effectively constrain conflicted creditors, lenders, managers, and other parties that use restructuring rights for private advantage?
themes.definition: This question examines whether courts can identify and police strategic behavior without excessively interfering with legitimate bargaining and creditor rights.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy courts be centralized in specialized venues, or should venue competition and decentralized administration improve Chapter 11 outcomes?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how institutional design, court specialization, and venue selection affect fairness, expertise, predictability, and efficiency in large cases.

themes.name: Is a uniform Chapter 11 regime suitable for heterogeneous firms and increasingly complex financial structures?
themes.definition: This question considers whether different types of businesses require tailored insolvency procedures rather than a single statutory framework.

themes.name: Do procedural protections and demands for finality improve Chapter 11 legitimacy, or do they make reorganization slower and more costly?
themes.definition: This question assesses the tradeoff between protecting impaired parties from erroneous or coercive outcomes and enabling timely resolution of distressed businesses.

themes.name: Does legal uncertainty in bankruptcy discourage efficient distressed-business transactions and increase valuation and distribution disputes?
themes.definition: This question examines how uncertain doctrine, judicial decision-making, and disputed rights affect the cost, timing, and design of reorganizations.

themes.name: Does bankruptcy law create incentives that influence managerial behavior, creditor contracting, and the timing of filing?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how ex ante legal rules and ex post restructuring powers shape risk-taking, early intervention, strategic delay, and private responses to distress.

themes.name: Should Chapter 11 be judged by aggregate value maximization alone, or also by fairness, vulnerability, and broader social consequences?
themes.definition: This question challenges narrow efficiency-based assessments by asking whether bankruptcy should protect noncontrolling stakeholders and public or relational interests even at some cost to financial recoveries.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy law enforce contractual priority and secured-creditor rights when doing so reduces recoveries or bargaining power for unsecured creditors?
themes.definition: This question examines whether contractual priority, security interests, and statutory exceptions should prevail over bankruptcy’s equality and collective-distribution objectives.

themes.name: Do pervasive secured-creditor rights preserve going-concern value, or do they enable lender control and premature liquidation of viable firms?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether secured lenders’ enforcement powers and collateral protections improve reorganizations or instead undermine enterprise preservation.

themes.name: When may bankruptcy courts depart from ordinary priority and equality rules to promote reorganization or protect particular claimants?
themes.definition: This question concerns the legal and normative limits of exceptions, unequal treatment, and nonconsensual redistributions in bankruptcy.

themes.name: Can private contracts modify or bypass mandatory Bankruptcy Code rules without defeating collective bankruptcy objectives?
themes.definition: This question analyzes the boundary between private ordering and mandatory bankruptcy law, including contractual waivers, restructuring agreements, and rights created outside bankruptcy.

themes.name: How should courts resolve ambiguous Bankruptcy Code provisions when statutory text conflicts with bankruptcy policy or practical consequences?
