themes.definition: This question evaluates whether managers and incumbent constituencies should retain authority after filing and what safeguards are needed against conflicts and fiduciary failure.

themes.name: Should managers’ and directors’ duties change when a corporation becomes insolvent or enters Chapter 11?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether insolvency should shift fiduciary responsibilities or decision-making authority toward creditors and other affected constituencies.

themes.name: Can private contracting efficiently replace mandatory bankruptcy rules for coordinating creditors in financial distress?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether sophisticated parties can anticipate and contract around insolvency contingencies without undermining collective recovery or protecting vulnerable parties.

themes.name: Do bankruptcy’s collective procedures legitimately alter nondebtor parties’ contractual and property rights?
themes.definition: This question examines the permissible effect of the automatic stay, assumption or rejection, discharge, and related doctrines on parties outside the bankruptcy estate.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy courts have equitable authority to modify nonbankruptcy liabilities and rights when strict enforcement threatens reorganization?
themes.definition: This question addresses the institutional and doctrinal limits on courts’ ability to affect state-law obligations, third parties, and interests beyond the debtor’s estate.

themes.name: Do bankruptcy courts and plan-confirmation standards adequately protect dispersed creditors and shareholders from strategic behavior?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether information asymmetry, holdouts, conflicts of interest, and voting procedures distort collective decision-making and distributions.

themes.name: Do delay, administrative expense, and legal uncertainty make Chapter 11 less valuable than nonbankruptcy restructuring alternatives?
themes.definition: This question compares the procedural costs and timing of formal bankruptcy with private workouts, foreclosure, and other methods of resolving financial distress.

themes.name: Can specialized bankruptcy procedures resolve small-business or mass-liability cases more efficiently than ordinary Chapter 11?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether specialized institutions and streamlined processes reduce the costs and shortcomings of conventional reorganization without sacrificing stakeholder protections.

themes.name: Do judicial disagreement and ambiguous Bankruptcy Code provisions undermine predictable and coherent bankruptcy administration?
themes.definition: This question examines how statutory uncertainty, conflicting precedents, and inconsistent standards affect litigation, bargaining, and outcomes in reorganization cases.

themes.name: Does Chapter 11 preserve a distressed firm’s going-concern value better than liquidation or rapid asset sales?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether the reorganization process generates higher net value than liquidation or expedited sale after accounting for delay, administrative expense, and business disruption.

themes.name: Should incumbent owners and managers retain control of a Chapter 11 debtor when creditors would otherwise receive priority?
themes.definition: This question examines whether debtor-in-possession control and equity retention are justified by their rehabilitation benefits or instead create agency costs and unjustified wealth transfers.

themes.name: Should secured creditors’ state-law collateral and enforcement rights be modified to permit continued operation of the debtor?
themes.definition: This question addresses when bankruptcy may restrict liens, foreclosure, or collateral remedies in order to preserve enterprise value without improperly redistributing secured creditors’ entitlements.

themes.name: Should the absolute priority rule apply to restructurings and asset transactions conducted outside a conventional Chapter 11 plan?
themes.definition: This question tests whether equity retention and other distributions to junior stakeholders should be barred when senior claims are not fully satisfied, even if the transaction is structured as a sale or other non-plan mechanism.

themes.name: Do bankruptcy classification and equal-treatment rules fairly allocate scarce assets among similarly situated creditors?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether claim classification, priority, and distribution rules prevent discrimination while recognizing economically meaningful differences among creditors.

themes.name: How should bankruptcy law represent future, contingent, or otherwise unrepresented claimants?
themes.definition: This question asks whether conventional claims-administration and voting mechanisms adequately protect claimants whose injuries or entitlements are difficult to value or are not yet legally actionable.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy courts use equitable powers to override or reallocate prebankruptcy contractual and property rights?
themes.definition: This question examines the legitimacy and limits of judicially created exceptions when enforcing ordinary rights would conflict with collective insolvency objectives.

themes.name: Should ambiguous Bankruptcy Code provisions be resolved primarily through statutory text or through purpose, context, and legislative history?
themes.definition: This question compares formalist and purposive approaches to interpreting incomplete or conflicting bankruptcy statutes and assesses their effects on predictability and fairness.

themes.name: Do creditor participation and voting mechanisms promote collective creditor interests or enable individual holdouts and strategic obstruction?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether creditor committees, plan voting, objections, and exit rights improve collective decision-making or allow powerful creditors to extract private advantages.

themes.name: Do distressed-debt purchases and lender control strategies improve restructuring outcomes or facilitate opportunistic takeovers?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether trading claims, acquiring influence, and using bankruptcy financing to obtain control create efficient solutions or harm debtors and less powerful stakeholders.

themes.name: Are private workouts and alternative restructuring mechanisms more efficient than traditional court-supervised Chapter 11?
themes.definition: This question compares prepackaged cases, out-of-court restructurings, and other alternatives with full Chapter 11 proceedings on value preservation, cost, speed, and creditor protection.

themes.name: Does the speed of Chapter 11 restructuring undermine procedural safeguards for affected creditors and nondebtor parties?
themes.definition: This question examines whether expedited hearings, sales, and plan processes sacrifice notice, participation, accurate valuation, or fair adjudication.

themes.name: Should Chapter 11 permit reorganizations to modify or discharge ongoing contractual and legacy obligations?
themes.definition: This question evaluates when bankruptcy should impair executory contracts, pension and retiree obligations, or other continuing liabilities to facilitate rehabilitation.

themes.name: Do postpetition administrative claims and debtor-in-possession obligations allocate risk efficiently?
themes.definition: This question studies whether special priority for postpetition financing, goods, and services encourages continued operation without excessively diluting prepetition creditors.

themes.name: Should governance rights in bankruptcy track formal creditor status or stakeholders’ actual economic exposure?
themes.definition: This question asks whether voting, control, and representation should reflect legal claim classifications or the parties who genuinely bear the gains and losses from reorganization.

themes.name: Do bankruptcy rules create efficient ex ante incentives for lending, monitoring, management, and corporate governance?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how priority, control, liability, and reorganization rules affect financing and managerial behavior before financial distress occurs.

themes.name: Are bankruptcy professionals, debtors, and creditors adequately constrained by good-faith and accountability standards?
themes.definition: This question examines whether existing duties, sanctions, disclosure requirements, and judicial oversight deter misconduct and opportunistic behavior in bankruptcy cases.

themes.name: Do bankruptcy reforms intended to constrain insider benefits or creditor power achieve their goals without being circumvented?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether statutory and institutional reforms reduce inequitable control and compensation practices or instead generate avoidance strategies and unintended costs.

themes.name: Should Chapter 11 use different procedural and institutional designs for small, large, and unusually complex business debtors?
themes.definition: This question tests whether a unitary reorganization framework is appropriate across debtor types or whether differentiated procedures would improve court capacity, speed, and fairness.

themes.name: Does bankruptcy adequately protect public-interest and nondebtor stakeholders whose losses extend beyond ordinary creditor recoveries?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the treatment of retirees, tort claimants, communities, and other stakeholders whose interests may be weakly represented by conventional bankruptcy entitlements.

themes.name: Does Chapter 11 preserve going-concern value more effectively than liquidation while still protecting creditor recoveries?
themes.definition: This question examines whether reorganization produces greater overall value than forced liquidation without unfairly sacrificing creditor entitlements.

themes.name: Do secured and debtor-in-possession lenders exercise excessive control over Chapter 11 outcomes?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether lender financing and security rights improperly determine restructuring decisions, creditor recoveries, or the survival of the debtor.

themes.name: When may bankruptcy law override or modify prebankruptcy contractual and property rights?
themes.definition: This question concerns the permissible limits of bankruptcy courts and debtors in altering, subordinating, or discharging rights created before the petition.

themes.name: Does Chapter 11 allocate value fairly between secured creditors, unsecured creditors, equity holders, and other claimants?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether priority rules, valuation methods, and plan distributions produce justified outcomes among competing constituencies.

themes.name: Should collective bankruptcy procedures restrict individual creditor enforcement, holdouts, and preferential bargaining?
themes.definition: This question examines whether collective treatment of creditors improves total recoveries and equality without unduly depriving creditors of individually negotiated rights.

themes.name: How should managerial fiduciary duties and shareholder voting rights change as a corporation approaches insolvency?
themes.definition: This question asks whether control should shift from shareholders and managers toward creditors or other stakeholders when equity value is impaired.

themes.name: Do expedited Section 363 sales undermine Chapter 11’s creditor-protection and plan-confirmation safeguards?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether quick asset sales preserve value or instead bypass deliberative restructuring and redistribute value toward favored parties.

themes.name: How should bankruptcy treat executory contracts and nondebtor counterparties during reorganization?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether rejection, assumption, assignment, or modification of ongoing contracts appropriately balances debtor flexibility against counterparty protection.

themes.name: Should Chapter 11 include contingent future mass-tort claims whose injuries have not yet materialized?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether bankruptcy can fairly and effectively consolidate present and future liabilities while preserving an operating enterprise.

themes.name: Is formal bankruptcy more effective than consensual, contractual, or alternative restructuring procedures for financially distressed firms?
themes.definition: This question compares court-supervised bankruptcy with private workouts, receiverships, and other procedures in terms of efficiency, coordination, and creditor protection.

themes.name: Do bankruptcy rules create incentives for opportunistic filings, delay, forum manipulation, or strategic use of procedural protections?
themes.definition: This question examines whether participants exploit the structure of bankruptcy to obtain leverage or benefits unrelated to legitimate reorganization objectives.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy courts rely on equitable discretion or clearer categorical rules when the Bankruptcy Code is ambiguous?
themes.definition: This question addresses the tradeoff between flexible, context-sensitive adjudication and predictable statutory rules in resolving contested bankruptcy issues.

themes.name: Are bankruptcy courts institutionally equipped to resolve disputes extending beyond ordinary insolvency administration?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the jurisdiction, workload, authority, and institutional design of bankruptcy courts in handling complex legal and organizational disputes.

themes.name: Does corporate-bankruptcy venue shopping distort the administration and legitimacy of large Chapter 11 cases?
themes.definition: This question examines whether geographically remote or specialized venues affect judicial workload, stakeholder participation, procedural outcomes, or public confidence.

themes.name: Should preference law apply differently to Chapter 7 liquidations and Chapter 11 reorganizations?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether the recovery of prepetition transfers under Section 547 should depend on whether the debtor is liquidating or attempting to continue operations.

themes.name: Do bankruptcy valuation procedures fairly determine when equity holders are entitled to receive a recovery?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether uncertain enterprise valuations and new-value contributions accurately identify residual equity and prevent either overpayment or improper exclusion.

themes.name: Do disclosure, representation, and creditor-participation rules provide adequate oversight of Chapter 11 decision-making?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether creditors and other affected stakeholders receive enough information and institutional voice to monitor management, lenders, and proposed transactions.

themes.name: Should private contracts govern distressed-company relationships, or should mandatory bankruptcy rules redistribute control and value?
themes.definition: This question examines whether private ordering improves restructuring efficiency or instead enables powerful parties to impose inequitable outcomes on weaker stakeholders.

themes.name: Can bankruptcy proceedings appropriately address corporate wrongdoing and claims arising from a debtor’s prior conduct?
themes.definition: This question asks whether bankruptcy is a suitable forum for resolving liability and accountability claims without allowing insolvency to shield misconduct or overwhelm reorganization.

themes.name: Do existing Chapter 11 doctrines and institutions require structural reform to reflect modern restructuring practice?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether statutory rules, judicial interpretations, and bankruptcy institutions still accomplish their intended purposes given contemporary financing, case structures, and restructuring techniques.

themes.name: Does Chapter 11 preserve viable going concerns more effectively than liquidation or foreclosure?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether reorganization procedures generate or preserve enterprise value that would be lost through immediate liquidation or secured-creditor enforcement.

themes.name: Should Chapter 11 prioritize operating-business preservation over immediate creditor recoveries?
themes.definition: This question examines whether the rehabilitative and broader economic benefits of continued operations justify delaying or reducing near-term recoveries by creditors.

themes.name: How should secured-creditor control be limited when it threatens successful reorganization?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether liens, foreclosure rights, valuation advantages, or case-control powers of secured lenders should be adjusted to preserve enterprise value and unsecured recoveries.

themes.name: Does the absolute priority rule unfairly prevent junior stakeholders from sharing in going-concern value?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether equity holders or junior creditors should retain or receive value when senior claims are not fully satisfied in a reorganization.

themes.name: Can a rapid § 363 sale of substantially all operating assets legitimately substitute for a Chapter 11 plan?
themes.definition: This question examines whether expedited asset sales preserve value efficiently or improperly bypass plan-based voting, valuation, and distribution protections.

themes.name: How should bankruptcy courts value collateral and enterprise value when allocating recoveries?
themes.definition: This question concerns the legal and economic methods used to measure assets, going-concern surplus, and valuation risk among secured, unsecured, and equity claimants.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy override prebankruptcy contractual and state-law priorities to achieve collective insolvency objectives?
themes.definition: This question evaluates when federal bankruptcy policy may alter rights created by contracts, organizational arrangements, or nonbankruptcy law.

themes.name: How should the prepetition/postpetition boundary determine the treatment of bankruptcy-related claims?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether rights and liabilities arising around the filing date should be classified as prepetition claims, administrative obligations, or other protected interests.

themes.name: Are existing Chapter 11 confirmation standards adequate to test plan feasibility and fairness?
themes.definition: This question examines whether courts sufficiently scrutinize proposed plans for feasibility, lawful classification, creditor treatment, and realistic prospects of reorganization.

themes.name: Should confirmed Chapter 11 plans bind dissenting creditors despite disputes over entitlement or procedural legality?
themes.definition: This question addresses the tension between finality and collective resolution on one hand and objections based on legal entitlement, procedural defects, or substantive illegality on the other.

themes.name: How much equitable and discretionary authority should bankruptcy judges exercise in unusual cases?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether judicial flexibility is necessary to address under-specified circumstances or instead undermines statutory limits, predictability, and equal treatment.

themes.name: Do court-specific interpretations and bankruptcy professionals produce unjustified variation in Chapter 11 outcomes?
themes.definition: This question investigates how judges, attorneys, institutional actors, and local practices influence results beyond the formal requirements of the Bankruptcy Code.

themes.name: Does venue selection in large Chapter 11 cases create strategic advantages that distort bankruptcy administration?
themes.definition: This question examines why corporations select forums such as Delaware or the Southern District of New York and whether forum shopping affects consistency, creditor participation, or substantive outcomes.

themes.name: Do distressed-debt trading and fragmented claims improve or undermine collective bargaining in Chapter 11?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether claims trading, multiple affiliated claims, and strategic capital-structure fragmentation facilitate efficient negotiation or enable individual creditors to obtain disproportionate control.

themes.name: How should bankruptcy law allocate priority between secured lenders, administrative claimants, employees, and unsecured creditors?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether existing priority and classification rules fairly distribute limited estate value among creditors with different legal statuses and contributions.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy law recognize special rights or contractual arrangements that depart from ordinary distribution rules?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the legitimacy of subordination agreements, structured priority devices, creditor protections, and other arrangements that alter the statutory distribution scheme.

themes.name: Are bankruptcy courts and trustees adequately equipped to police conflicts of interest and creditor overreaching?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether legal and ethical controls sufficiently regulate debtors, trustees, professionals, lenders, bidders, and other participants whose conduct may impair estate value.

themes.name: Do collective bankruptcy procedures solve creditor-coordination problems without imposing excessive participation costs?
themes.definition: This question examines whether voting, claims procedures, procedural intervention, and centralized adjudication improve outcomes relative to private enforcement while avoiding unnecessary delay and expense.

themes.name: Should involuntary bankruptcy be used earlier to prevent debtor delay from destroying enterprise value?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether creditor-initiated proceedings provide a desirable intervention mechanism or create excessive risks of coercion and premature insolvency administration.

themes.name: Does Chapter 11’s flexibility improve efficient restructuring, or does it create unacceptable uncertainty and unequal treatment?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the tradeoff between adaptable procedures for complex distress and the need for predictable rules protecting creditor expectations, contractual rights, and legitimacy.

themes.name: Does debtor-in-possession financing preserve going-concern value without giving lenders excessive control over Chapter 11 cases?
themes.definition: This question examines whether special bankruptcy financing is necessary in constrained credit markets and whether its priority and governance effects unfairly shift power from other stakeholders.

themes.name: Should Chapter 11 control remain with the debtor, or shift to creditors and professional representatives when the debtor is financially distressed?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how control over corporate decisions should be allocated among debtor managers, lenders, bankruptcy courts, and other participants.

themes.name: Do bankruptcy valuation and adequate-protection rules fairly balance secured creditors’ enforcement rights against the debtor’s use of collateral?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether secured creditors receive sufficient protection when collateral is used, depreciates, generates proceeds, or remains subject to reorganization.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy preserve contractual creditor priorities, or permit mandatory redistribution to advance collective reorganization goals?
themes.definition: This question addresses when bankruptcy law should respect prebankruptcy priority arrangements and when it may override them to preserve value or protect other constituencies.

themes.name: Should equity holders retain value or bargaining leverage when the firm cannot satisfy its senior debt obligations?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether shareholders or other junior claimants should receive value, new equity, or procedural influence despite being economically out of the money.

themes.name: Can Chapter 11’s cramdown and creditor-classification rules fairly resolve conflicts among creditors with different legal and economic interests?
themes.definition: This question examines whether classification, voting, and cramdown mechanisms produce legitimate distributions rather than allowing selected creditor groups to control or evade collective outcomes.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy courts permit nonplan sales and other procedural devices that transfer value outside the ordinary Chapter 11 plan process?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether sale procedures and related mechanisms can preserve going-concern value without circumventing creditor voting, priority, disclosure, or distribution protections.

themes.name: Do bankruptcy procedures prevent powerful participants from using strategic bargaining to redistribute value away from less powerful creditors?
themes.definition: This question studies whether creditor activism, debtor-driven tactics, private agreements, and participation advantages undermine cooperative and value-maximizing resolution.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy law protect workers, tort claimants, pension beneficiaries, and other noncontractual constituencies against creditor-centered distributions?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether broader social and stakeholder interests justify departures from conventional creditor-priority and estate-maximization principles.

themes.name: Can Chapter 11 effectively estimate, settle, and collectively resolve numerous future or unliquidated tort claims?
themes.definition: This question examines whether bankruptcy procedures can provide fair and administrable treatment for dispersed claimants whose liabilities are uncertain at filing.

themes.name: When should bankruptcy law alter or extinguish nondebtor contractual rights and obligations involving intangible or use-based assets?
themes.definition: This question addresses how the legal characterization of licenses, contracts, rents, and other nontraditional arrangements determines whether they can be assumed, rejected, transferred, or terminated.

themes.name: Should federal bankruptcy law displace state-law remedies and private contractual arrangements when they conflict with collective reorganization?
themes.definition: This question concerns the proper boundary between federal bankruptcy governance, state corporate and property law, and privately negotiated creditor rights.

themes.name: Does filing for Chapter 11 justify replacing ordinary state corporate governance with federal bankruptcy governance?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether insolvency should trigger expanded federal control over corporate decision-making, fiduciary obligations, and stakeholder relationships.

themes.name: Are open-ended fairness standards preferable to categorical rules for resolving ambiguous and contested Bankruptcy Code provisions?
themes.definition: This question compares flexible judicial assessments with formal doctrinal categories in terms of predictability, legitimacy, creditor protection, and adaptability.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy courts develop doctrines to fill statutory gaps, or should unresolved Chapter 11 issues be left to Congress?
themes.definition: This question examines the institutional legitimacy and practical consequences of judicial lawmaking, appellate interpretation, and incremental statutory development in bankruptcy.

themes.name: Does the institutional design of Chapter 11 produce efficient and predictable outcomes, or excessive delay, cost, and judicial discretion?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the resource demands, timing, caseload capacity, procedural flexibility, and legitimacy of court-supervised reorganization.

themes.name: Do bankruptcy courts’ competition for large cases undermine impartial administration and coherent national bankruptcy policy?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether venue competition for mega-cases affects judicial incentives, stakeholder outcomes, and consistency across bankruptcy courts.

themes.name: Does Chapter 11 preserve viable going-concern value better than liquidation, or merely delay liquidation and redistribute losses?
themes.definition: This question compares reorganization’s purported rehabilitation benefits with its costs, delays, value transfers, and ability to maintain productive assets and relationships.

themes.name: Are out-of-court workouts and alternative restructuring procedures more efficient than conventional Chapter 11 proceedings for resolving corporate distress?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether consensual negotiations, distressed-debt transactions, or redesigned insolvency mechanisms can reduce costs while preserving collective protections.

themes.name: Do bankruptcy rules create incentives for managers, creditors, or insiders to behave opportunistically rather than maximize the distressed firm’s total value?
themes.definition: This question examines how priority rules, control rights, conflicts of interest, and bankruptcy-related powers shape strategic behavior before and during reorganization.

themes.name: Does debtor-in-possession control create agency-cost and power asymmetries that distort Chapter 11 outcomes?
themes.definition: This question examines whether allowing incumbent managers to retain control systematically advantages debtors or insiders over creditors, employees, and other bankruptcy stakeholders.

themes.name: Should Chapter 11 prioritize preserving viable going concerns over rapid asset sales or liquidation?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether reorganization law and bankruptcy sales should protect operating-business value when continuation may produce greater value than immediate liquidation.

themes.name: Do expedited or preplanned Chapter 11 procedures sacrifice necessary creditor and stakeholder protections?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether speed, prepackaged resolutions, and shortened objection periods improve restructuring efficiency at the cost of meaningful participation and procedural fairness.

themes.name: Is Chapter 11’s existing institutional design effective enough to justify limiting major statutory reform?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether the Bankruptcy Code and its institutions successfully rehabilitate viable firms, liquidate nonviable ones, and distribute value fairly compared with proposed alternatives.

themes.name: How should Chapter 11 allocate control among debtor management, secured creditors, junior creditors, and shareholders?
themes.definition: This question investigates which participants should possess decision-making authority during reorganization when their incentives and claims to value conflict.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy preserve ordinary contractual and state-law creditor priorities or modify them to advance reorganization objectives?
themes.definition: This question addresses the tension between prebankruptcy entitlements and bankruptcy’s collective, value-preserving, and distributional purposes.

themes.name: Does the automatic stay appropriately balance debtor protection against secured creditors’ enforcement rights?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether the stay gives distressed firms necessary breathing space without unfairly impairing secured lenders’ property and control rights.

themes.name: Can private financing and contractual arrangements evade mandatory bankruptcy protections?
themes.definition: This question examines whether sophisticated transactions, covenants, refinancing structures, or anti-assignment provisions can circumvent the automatic stay, collective proceedings, or creditor protections.

themes.name: Are out-of-plan asset sales being used to circumvent Chapter 11’s plan-based protections?
themes.definition: This question asks whether rapid or court-approved sales improperly replace a reorganization process and deprive junior creditors and other parties of valuation and voting rights.

themes.name: When may Chapter 11 bind dissenting, unknown, or nonconsenting creditors?
themes.definition: This question concerns the legal and normative limits of imposing restructuring terms on claimants who did not agree to them or cannot be individually identified.

themes.name: Does the absolute-priority rule fairly determine whether distressed shareholders may retain value or be eliminated without compensation?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how Chapter 11 should treat prebankruptcy equity holders when creditor claims exceed the firm’s value.

themes.name: Do priority rules and creditor classifications produce justified distributions among senior, junior, secured, and unsecured claimants?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether formal priority, classification, and judicially created exceptions allocate value consistently with contractual expectations and bankruptcy policy.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy remedies give special protection to tort victims and other less powerful stakeholders even when doing so reduces creditor recoveries?
themes.definition: This question examines whether finality, estate-value maximization, and creditor equality should yield to the interests of tort claimants, employees, communities, or other socially favored groups.

themes.name: Do debt financing and creditor-control arrangements preserve distressed firms or intensify their decline?
themes.definition: This question studies whether postpetition financing, debt covenants, and lender control improve business survival or encourage premature liquidation and value transfers.

themes.name: How do managerial and shareholder incentives before insolvency affect later bankruptcy risk and distributional outcomes?
themes.definition: This question links corporate control, risk-taking, and strategic decisions before filing to conflicts among insiders, creditors, and other stakeholders during bankruptcy.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy courts exercise broader discretion to police strategic behavior and inequitable creditor arrangements?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether judicial intervention is needed to constrain self-interested bargaining, creditor coordination failures, and transactions that exploit procedural or doctrinal gaps.

themes.name: Are bankruptcy courts institutionally capable of resolving complex reorganizations and enforcing equitable limits on private arrangements?
themes.definition: This question assesses the proper scope of bankruptcy judges’ discretion, statutory interpretation, procedural supervision, and competence in large or innovative cases.

themes.name: Does forum shopping, particularly in specialized or geographically remote bankruptcy courts, affect the legitimacy and substance of Chapter 11 outcomes?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether venue selection and the role of courts such as Delaware’s specialized bankruptcy tribunals influence rules, bargaining power, and stakeholder treatment.

themes.name: Do disclosure and professional-compensation rules adequately control information and agency problems in Chapter 11?
themes.definition: This question examines whether disclosure requirements, attorneys’ fees, and other professional-oversight mechanisms make reorganization negotiations transparent and accountable.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy law rely more on precise standardized rules or on flexible judicial and negotiated solutions?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether clearer procedures and statutory standards would improve predictability and legitimacy or instead undermine context-sensitive responses to heterogeneous distressed firms.

themes.name: Do DIP-financing terms give secured lenders excessive control over Chapter 11 reorganizations?
themes.definition: This question examines whether priority, collateral, and governance provisions in debtor-in-possession financing enable lenders to redirect or constrain the debtor’s reorganization beyond what is necessary to preserve value.

themes.name: When may bankruptcy courts depart from apparently mandatory statutory rights on equitable or policy grounds?
themes.definition: This question concerns the permissible scope of judicial discretion when Bankruptcy Code text conflicts with fairness, bankruptcy policy, or the practical needs of a particular case.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy courts prioritize statutory text over bankruptcy history, congressional purpose, and equitable outcomes?
themes.definition: This question evaluates competing methods of interpreting ambiguous or conflicting Bankruptcy Code provisions.

themes.name: Does the absolute priority rule produce efficient and fair allocations of value in corporate reorganizations?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether priority for senior claims appropriately protects creditor expectations and incentives without unnecessarily preventing valuable settlements or continued operations.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy law restrict secured creditors’ foreclosure, governance, and control rights during financial distress?
themes.definition: This question examines whether secured lenders’ prebankruptcy rights should be limited when exercising them could destroy going-concern value or undermine collective reorganization.

themes.name: How should collateral value and postpetition charges determine the treatment of secured creditors in Chapter 11?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether secured collateral should bear administrative expenses and how valuation should affect adequate protection, plan distributions, and creditor influence.

themes.name: When is reorganization more efficient than liquidation, sale, or dismissal for a financially distressed business?
themes.definition: This question compares resolution methods by asking whether continued operation preserves more enterprise value than converting or selling the debtor’s assets.

themes.name: Do expedited or nonplan asset sales preserve enterprise value at the cost of stakeholder protections?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether Chapter 11 sales conducted outside the ordinary plan process generate efficient outcomes or enable coercion, procedural evasion, and distributional transfers.

themes.name: How should debtor-in-possession managers’ discretion be constrained when managers control the reorganization?
themes.definition: This question examines the allocation of authority and fiduciary responsibility among managers, shareholders, creditors, and courts during a debtor-controlled case.

themes.name: Does Chapter 11’s collective process protect overall creditor recoveries better than individual enforcement rights?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether centralized administration and limits on individual remedies solve coordination problems without unfairly suppressing creditor-specific entitlements.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy maximize estate value even when doing so alters prebankruptcy contractual or state-law rights?
themes.definition: This question tests the legitimacy of prioritizing aggregate or going-concern value over the preservation of private entitlements created before bankruptcy.

themes.name: When should federal bankruptcy law override state-law arrangements and nonbankruptcy contractual rights?
themes.definition: This question concerns the substantive, constitutional, and policy limits on using bankruptcy law to modify rights otherwise governed by state or commercial law.

themes.name: How should bankruptcy treat executory contracts, commercial leases, and nondebtor counterparties whose rights impede reorganization?
themes.definition: This question examines when the estate may assume, reject, assign, or alter ongoing contractual relationships despite nonbankruptcy restrictions and counterparty interests.

themes.name: Should obligations arising from prebankruptcy conduct be treated as bankruptcy claims subject to distribution and discharge?
themes.definition: This question addresses the boundary between a bankruptcy claim and an enforceable nonbankruptcy remedy, including uncertainty about future or contingent claims.

themes.name: How far should bankruptcy-court jurisdiction extend over nondebtor parties and peripheral disputes?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether bankruptcy courts may adjudicate matters involving entities, rights, or controversies only indirectly connected to the debtor’s estate.

themes.name: Do bankruptcy procedures adequately balance speed, transaction costs, participation, and creditor protection?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether procedural design and judicial practice make reorganizations sufficiently rapid and inexpensive without sacrificing legitimacy or affected parties’ rights.

themes.name: Does strategic use of bankruptcy allow debtors or creditors to obtain advantages unrelated to genuine insolvency?
themes.definition: This question examines strategic timing, venue selection, insider conduct, and use of Chapter 11 tools to produce bargaining or distributional advantages.

themes.name: Can private or expedited restructuring mechanisms substitute for formal Chapter 11 without sacrificing collective protections?
themes.definition: This question compares consensual, contractual, and out-of-court mechanisms with formal bankruptcy proceedings as methods of coordinating creditors and preserving distressed firms.

themes.name: Does judicial oversight adequately control professional fees, creditor-debtor arrangements, and coercive restructuring bargains?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether courts effectively supervise attorneys, advisers, lenders, and negotiated case arrangements to prevent overreaching and unnecessary bankruptcy costs.

themes.name: Do empirical evidence and debtor heterogeneity justify reforming generally applicable Chapter 11 rules?
themes.definition: This question asks whether observed differences among distressed firms and actual case outcomes undermine broad assumptions about bankruptcy efficiency and support targeted legal reform.

themes.name: Does Chapter 11 preserve viable firms more effectively than liquidation-oriented alternatives?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether Chapter 11 produces greater going-concern value and successful rehabilitation than faster liquidation or claim-rearrangement procedures.

themes.name: Do Chapter 11’s delay and expense undermine the value of reorganization?
themes.definition: This question examines whether procedural cost, delay, and administrative complexity turn Chapter 11 into an inefficient substitute for liquidation.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy law prioritize secured creditors’ contractual rights over the collective interests of the estate?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether secured lenders’ enforcement and in-rem rights should prevail when they conflict with preserving estate value or protecting junior stakeholders.

themes.name: Does creditor control after default improve reorganizations or enable coercive value redistribution?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether creditor influence over corporate decisions produces value-maximizing outcomes or allows powerful creditors to extract unfair advantages.

themes.name: How should bankruptcy priority rules resolve conflicts between senior, junior, unsecured, and equity claimants?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether formal priority and pro rata distribution rules allocate insolvency losses fairly when competing claims and policy considerations collide.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy courts permit departures from formal priority rules to prevent severe or socially harmful outcomes?
themes.definition: This question considers when equitable or policy-based exceptions to ordinary priority should be allowed despite the risk of unpredictability and preferential treatment.

themes.name: Do contractual devices improperly circumvent bankruptcy’s collective distribution scheme?
themes.definition: This question examines whether loan provisions, intercreditor agreements, entity structures, and related transactions allow parties to obtain bankruptcy advantages unavailable under default rules.

themes.name: How should bankruptcy law modify pre-bankruptcy contractual rights?
themes.definition: This question concerns the proper limits on enforcing, discharging, or altering contractual rights and remedies after a bankruptcy petition is filed.

themes.name: Does the treatment of executory contracts under Bankruptcy Code § 365 efficiently balance estate value and counterparty protection?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether assumption, rejection, and assignment rules appropriately preserve valuable contracts without unfairly burdening nondebtor counterparties.

themes.name: When should bankruptcy protections restrict foreclosure and other secured-creditor remedies?
themes.definition: This question asks whether foreclosure, repossession, or other creditor-initiated transfers should proceed despite the collective protections triggered by bankruptcy.

themes.name: Does bankruptcy filing appropriately shift corporate control from managers and equity holders to creditors and the court?
themes.definition: This question examines whether the legal consequences of filing adequately respond to changed incentives while preserving managers’ ability to operate a viable business.

themes.name: Do creditor monitoring and liability rules constrain managers’ opportunism during financial distress?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether creditor oversight, fiduciary duties, and legal liability induce distressed-firm managers to make value-maximizing decisions.

themes.name: Should junior creditors’ procedural and litigation rights be restricted to facilitate efficient reorganization?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether limiting challenges, discovery, voting, or participation by junior claimants improves coordination without suppressing legitimate protection against overreach.

themes.name: How much discretion should bankruptcy judges have when statutory rules do not clearly resolve a dispute?
themes.definition: This question addresses the tradeoff between context-sensitive judicial intervention and predictable, rule-based protection of legal entitlements.

themes.name: Are bankruptcy courts exceeding their authority by resolving disputes governed by state or nonbankruptcy law?
themes.definition: This question examines the constitutional and statutory boundary between federal bankruptcy jurisdiction and state-law property, contract, corporate-governance, or nondebtor rights.

themes.name: Do court-approved extraordinary arrangements produce comprehensive and efficient restructurings?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether nonstandard Chapter 11 mechanisms and judicially approved settlements solve complex liabilities more effectively than ordinary litigation or decentralized bargaining.

themes.name: Can Chapter 11 effectively resolve mass-tort liabilities while preserving the debtor as a going concern?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether bankruptcy can combine business preservation with a fair and comprehensive settlement of claims held by dispersed tort victims.

themes.name: Does bankruptcy’s collective process outperform decentralized creditor enforcement?
themes.definition: This question compares collective bankruptcy administration with individual collection, foreclosure, or litigation in preventing creditor races and maximizing aggregate recoveries.

themes.name: Do bankruptcy procedures adequately protect unsecured creditors while maximizing estate value?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether unsecured creditors receive meaningful representation and recoveries without imposing procedures that destroy the estate’s value.

themes.name: Do venue selection and judicial practice materially affect Chapter 11 outcomes?
themes.definition: This question uses empirical comparisons across courts, including prominent bankruptcy venues, to determine whether forum choice changes case duration, creditor recoveries, or restructuring results.

themes.name: Should Chapter 11 restrict secured creditors’ foreclosure and enforcement rights to preserve going-concern value?
themes.definition: This question examines when bankruptcy’s collective reorganization process should override secured creditors’ state-law property, reclamation, and foreclosure rights.

themes.name: Can senior secured or debtor-in-possession lenders use financial leverage to force inefficient asset sales?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether lender control, financing terms, or collateral rights enable powerful creditors to extract value through premature liquidation.

themes.name: Who should control corporate decision-making during Chapter 11?
themes.definition: This question compares managerial, creditor, shareholder, court, and market control over the debtor’s operations and restructuring decisions.

themes.name: Does Chapter 11 preserve viable firms more effectively than liquidation or rapid asset sales?
themes.definition: This question tests whether court-supervised reorganization creates more economic value than liquidation, foreclosure, or expedited sales of distressed assets.

themes.name: Should Chapter 11 procedures be simplified or differentiated to reduce the costs and delays of reorganization?
themes.definition: This question asks whether speed, transaction costs, and administrative burdens justify streamlined procedures or different rules for different types and sizes of debtors.

themes.name: How far should bankruptcy courts’ authority extend beyond the debtor’s core estate?
themes.definition: This question concerns the constitutional and statutory limits on courts’ power to restrict conduct, resolve disputes, or affect rights involving non-debtors and assets outside the estate.

themes.name: Should ambiguous Bankruptcy Code provisions be resolved through broad purposive interpretation or strict statutory textualism?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how courts should interpret poorly drafted, ambiguous, or conflicting Code provisions and whether judicial interpretation should be supplemented by agency rulemaking.

themes.name: When should bankruptcy law override state-law property rights, anti-assignment clauses, and private contracts?
themes.definition: This question examines the boundary between federal bankruptcy entitlements and prebankruptcy contractual or nonbankruptcy-law rights.

themes.name: How should Chapter 11 allocate value among secured creditors, unsecured creditors, and shareholders?
themes.definition: This question addresses priority, valuation, bargaining power, cramdown, and the permissible redistribution of value among competing claimant classes.

themes.name: Do existing Chapter 11 mechanisms adequately protect unsecured, subordinate, and dispersed creditors?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether parties with weak bargaining power receive meaningful representation, information, and recovery during corporate reorganizations.

themes.name: How should Chapter 11 handle mass-tort and other claims that are not fixed monetary obligations?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether bankruptcy can fairly and efficiently aggregate, estimate, prioritize, and resolve contingent, future, or non-monetary claims.

themes.name: Should creditor value maximization yield to protection for employees and other vulnerable stakeholders?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how bankruptcy should balance estate maximization and investor recovery against unpaid wages, workers, and diffuse noninvestor interests.

themes.name: Can private prebankruptcy agreements and negotiated restructurings replace mandatory Chapter 11 without undermining creditor protection?
themes.definition: This question examines whether prepackaged, out-of-court, or market-based arrangements produce more efficient outcomes than formal proceedings while protecting nonconsenting parties.

themes.name: How should bankruptcy law resolve collective-action and coordination problems among competing creditors?
themes.definition: This question studies whether collective proceedings, voting rules, stays, and institutional mechanisms prevent individual creditors from gaining at the expense of the creditor body.

themes.name: Do bankruptcy rules create efficient incentives for firms and creditors before financial distress?
themes.definition: This question examines how filing rules, preference liability, creditor monitoring, lending terms, and debtor conduct affect behavior before and near insolvency.

themes.name: Can specialized fiduciaries and bankruptcy professionals improve decision-making enough to justify their costs?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether trustees, examiners, independent directors, attorneys, experts, and other professionals mitigate conflicts and uncertainty in exchange for acceptable administrative expense.

themes.name: How should courts distinguish legitimate reorganization from strategic or abusive use of Chapter 11?
themes.definition: This question concerns judicial standards for identifying filings, transactions, and procedural tactics that pursue genuine rehabilitation rather than opportunistic delay or value extraction.

themes.name: Does Chapter 11’s institutional design effectively resolve corporate financial distress?
themes.definition: This question empirically evaluates whether Chapter 11 procedures preserve value, resolve competing claims, and produce successful reorganizations at reasonable cost.

themes.name: Is the Bankruptcy Code adequate for complex modern financial arrangements and changing corporate structures?
themes.definition: This question asks whether traditional bankruptcy doctrines and the 1978 Code remain suitable for sophisticated contracts, novel capital structures, and contemporary forms of enterprise.

themes.name: Can efficiency or wealth maximization provide an adequate normative foundation for bankruptcy law?
themes.definition: This question tests whether bankruptcy institutions can be justified primarily by economic efficiency or must also incorporate fairness, entitlement protection, rehabilitation, and broader social objectives.

themes.name: Do secured creditors effectively control the debtor and major decisions during Chapter 11?
themes.definition: This question examines whether liens, financing rights, creditor agreements, and court practices allow senior lenders to displace directors, managers, or other stakeholders in governing the reorganization.

themes.name: Should Chapter 11 prioritize preserving viable businesses as going concerns over maximizing immediate creditor recoveries?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether continuation of the enterprise produces greater overall value than liquidation, asset sales, or rapid value extraction by creditors.

themes.name: Does Chapter 11’s institutional design produce efficient and successful reorganizations?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether Chapter 11’s procedures, incentives, timing, and allocation of authority reliably preserve value and resolve financially distressed firms.

themes.name: Does competition among bankruptcy courts encourage inefficient venue shopping in large Chapter 11 cases?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether district-level competition to attract major cases changes legal outcomes, procedural practices, or the fairness of reorganizations.

themes.name: How should courts interpret ambiguous Bankruptcy Code provisions: through formal text, statutory purpose, or equitable principles?
themes.definition: This question concerns the competing interpretive methods courts use when the Code does not clearly determine the status, rights, or treatment of a bankruptcy claim or transaction.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy courts replace case-specific discretion with clearer and more uniform standards?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether predictable rules would improve legitimacy and consistency or instead prevent courts from adapting bankruptcy procedures to unusual debtors and creditor relationships.

themes.name: Are collective bankruptcy procedures necessary to prevent creditor grab races, holdouts, and disproportionate individual recoveries?
themes.definition: This question examines whether centralized bankruptcy intervention produces better outcomes than decentralized enforcement by individual creditors.

themes.name: How should Chapter 11 allocate priority among secured creditors, unsecured creditors, shareholders, and other claimants?
themes.definition: This question addresses the classification, ranking, and distributional treatment of competing claims and ownership interests in reorganization.

themes.name: Does the absolute priority rule adequately prevent owners from retaining value when creditors are not fully paid?
themes.definition: This question focuses on whether consent, valuation disputes, or other Chapter 11 mechanisms improperly allow equity holders to retain interests despite unpaid senior claims.

themes.name: Should managers or creditors control consequential decisions in a financially distressed corporation?
themes.definition: This question evaluates how voting rights, creditor influence, managerial authority, and shareholder-creditor conflicts should be allocated during distress and reorganization.

themes.name: Is bankruptcy-court oversight sufficient to prevent debtor, lender, and professional participants from redistributing value opportunistically?
themes.definition: This question examines whether courts adequately police transactions and strategies that transfer value among preexisting stakeholders without increasing enterprise value.

themes.name: Do expedited and non-plan Chapter 11 mechanisms undermine collective decision-making and creditor protections?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether quick sales, settlements, releases, and other mechanisms outside a conventional plan sacrifice scrutiny, voting, and protection for dissenting or third-party interests.

themes.name: Do Chapter 11 asset sales preserve going-concern value or facilitate undervalued transfers to favored buyers or creditors?
themes.definition: This question concerns the valuation, governance, and distributional consequences of selling a debtor’s business or assets during reorganization.

themes.name: How should Chapter 11 balance the debtor’s need to restructure contracts against the rights of non-debtor counterparties?
themes.definition: This question examines rejection, assumption, assignment, and continued performance of executory contracts and leases when bankruptcy powers conflict with contractual protections.

themes.name: Do debtor-in-possession financing and lender-proposed restructuring arrangements give secured lenders excessive leverage?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether financing terms, milestones, liens, and limited-market conditions allow lenders to control the case or extract value at the expense of other stakeholders.

themes.name: Do bankruptcy rules create incentives for strategic behavior that reduce the value available to the creditor body?
themes.definition: This question investigates opportunistic conduct by debtors, creditors, managers, investors, and professionals, including hold-up, forum manipulation, and wealth transfers.

themes.name: Should entity-based bankruptcy-remoteness and withdrawal arrangements be respected over collective bankruptcy policies?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether special-purpose entities, separateness provisions, and contractual restrictions on placing assets or liabilities in bankruptcy should remain effective in insolvency.

themes.name: How should federal bankruptcy law interact with state-law property, contract, and liability regimes?
themes.definition: This question examines when federal bankruptcy powers should modify, displace, or defer to nonbankruptcy legal rights and state-law institutions.

themes.name: Are Chapter 11 procedures adequately designed for financially distressed small and medium-sized businesses?
themes.definition: This question tests whether the cost, complexity, timing, and institutional assumptions of Chapter 11 make reorganization inaccessible or ineffective for non-large-business debtors.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy law intervene earlier or use alternatives to conventional Chapter 11 for viable distressed firms?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether early intervention, negotiated restructuring, specialized processes, or other mechanisms outperform formal Chapter 11 in preserving enterprise value.

themes.name: Does Chapter 11 preserve going-concern value better than liquidation or expedited asset sales?
themes.definition: This question examines whether court-supervised reorganization preserves distressed firms and their assets or instead destroys value through delay, cost, or premature liquidation.

themes.name: How should control of a Chapter 11 debtor be divided among incumbent managers, creditors, and the bankruptcy court?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether managerial control, creditor participation, and judicial intervention are allocated in a way that limits agency problems while preserving effective reorganization.

themes.name: Can collective bankruptcy proceedings solve creditor-coordination problems better than individual enforcement or private bargaining?
themes.definition: This question compares centralized bankruptcy administration with separate creditor action and negotiated solutions in cases involving dispersed or conflicting creditors.

themes.name: When should secured creditors receive relief from the automatic stay or retain foreclosure rights during reorganization?
themes.definition: This question addresses how bankruptcy should balance secured creditors’ enforcement and collateral-recovery rights against the debtor’s need for time to reorganize.

themes.name: How should Chapter 11 distribute reorganized value among secured creditors, unsecured creditors, and equity holders?
themes.definition: This question examines priority, valuation, and allocation rules governing recoveries among creditor classes and shareholders in reorganizations.

themes.name: Should contractual arrangements be permitted to alter statutory bankruptcy priorities and distributional rules?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether subordination agreements, priority-structuring devices, or other private contracts should be enforceable when they conflict with bankruptcy’s default distribution scheme.

themes.name: To what extent should bankruptcy preserve prebankruptcy property, contractual, and state-law entitlements?
themes.definition: This question considers when bankruptcy should respect existing rights and transactions and when collective insolvency goals justify modifying or overriding them.

themes.name: How should Chapter 11 treat executory contracts, leases, and other specialized commercial relationships?
themes.definition: This question examines whether bankruptcy rules for assumption, rejection, termination, or modification of ongoing relationships appropriately allocate value and risk between debtors and counterparties.

themes.name: Should courts interpret ambiguous Bankruptcy Code provisions through textual rules or bankruptcy policy and equitable consequences?
themes.definition: This question compares plain-meaning, structural, legislative-history, and policy-oriented approaches to determining the scope of contested bankruptcy protections.

themes.name: When may bankruptcy courts depart from statutory default rules to achieve equitable or creditor-benefiting outcomes?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the legitimacy and limits of judicial discretion to approve nonstandard procedures, remedies, or distributions when conventional bankruptcy mechanisms are inadequate.

themes.name: How should Chapter 11 distinguish legitimate strategic conduct from abusive use of bankruptcy protections?
themes.definition: This question addresses good-faith filing, opportunistic use of Chapter 11, manipulation of creditor consent, and attempts to evade statutory distributions or obligations.

themes.name: Do claims-classification, voting, and plan-confirmation rules produce representative and legitimate reorganization outcomes?
themes.definition: This question examines whether formal participation and voting mechanisms accurately represent affected constituencies and constrain domination by powerful creditor groups.

themes.name: Does Chapter 11 adequately protect unsecured, tort, future-payment, and otherwise weakly represented creditors?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether priority, valuation, voting, and procedural rules prevent financially sophisticated parties from externalizing losses onto vulnerable claimants.

themes.name: Do postpetition financing and secured-creditor protections improve reorganization or allow lenders to obtain disproportionate control?
themes.definition: This question studies how financing constraints, valuation uncertainty, lender behavior, and debtor dependence on existing creditors affect Chapter 11 outcomes.

themes.name: Can streamlined Chapter 11 procedures reduce restructuring costs without sacrificing creditor and stakeholder protections?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether expedited processes, standardized rules, and limits on litigation or administration produce net efficiency gains rather than under-protecting affected parties.

themes.name: How should bankruptcy balance creditor recoveries against employment, business relationships, and broader economic effects?
themes.definition: This question examines whether bankruptcy policy should pursue objectives beyond estate-value maximization when reorganization or liquidation affects employees, communities, counterparties, or other nondebtor stakeholders.

themes.name: How should authority be divided between bankruptcy courts and state, corporate, commercial, or foreign legal institutions?
themes.definition: This question addresses federalism, jurisdictional overlap, cross-border coordination, and institutional competence in determining restructuring rights and procedures.

themes.name: Is corporate bankruptcy necessary when private contracts, corporate law, or nonjudicial insolvency mechanisms can address financial distress?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the proper scope of corporate bankruptcy and whether centralized judicial intervention solves problems that organizational law or private bargaining already handle.

themes.name: Do bankruptcy professionals and specialized bankruptcy courts improve case outcomes enough to justify their agency costs and institutional influence?
themes.definition: This question examines whether judges, trustees, attorneys, financial advisers, and specialized court structures enhance administration and valuation or instead distort incentives and creditor protection.

themes.name: Does the existing U.S. Chapter 11 framework remain institutionally efficient for modern and complex business failures?
themes.definition: This question uses historical, empirical, and institutional analysis to assess whether contemporary bankruptcy rules, procedures, and governance structures require legislative or doctrinal reform.

themes.name: Does Chapter 11 preserve more value as a going concern than liquidation or expedited asset sales?
themes.definition: This question examines when continued operation, traditional plan-based reorganization, or quicker asset-sale procedures best preserve enterprise value while protecting creditors.

themes.name: Are out-of-court workouts more effective than court-supervised bankruptcy for resolving corporate financial distress?
themes.definition: This question compares private workouts, negotiated restructurings, and formal bankruptcy proceedings in terms of efficiency, creditor coordination, coercion, and value preservation.

themes.name: When should bankruptcy law permit departures from absolute priority and equal-treatment rules?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether junior stakeholders or selected creditors may retain value despite senior or equal-ranking claims, and what legal or economic limits should apply.

themes.name: Do secured-creditor rights and first- versus second-lien priorities give senior lenders excessive control over Chapter 11 outcomes?
themes.definition: This question investigates how collateral rights, foreclosure remedies, lien priority, and creditor control affect reorganizations and distributions among secured and unsecured creditors.

themes.name: Can a Chapter 11 plan fairly bind dissenting, absent, or nonparticipating creditors?
themes.definition: This question assesses the legitimacy and limits of collective plan confirmation, cramdown, creditor voting, and procedures that bind claimants who do not consent.

themes.name: Does leaving existing management in control of a bankrupt firm produce efficient reorganization or unacceptable governance conflicts?
themes.definition: This question examines debtor-in-possession control, managerial incentives, fiduciary duties, and judicial oversight of debtor-controlled decisions.

themes.name: How much discretion should bankruptcy courts have to resolve novel disputes and fill gaps in the Bankruptcy Code?
themes.definition: This question addresses the balance between flexible, equitable adjudication and clear categorical rules in cases involving ambiguous statutes, incomplete agreements, or unusual facts.

themes.name: Should statutory text or bankruptcy policy control when interpreting ambiguous provisions governing creditor and property rights?
themes.definition: This question examines the relative weight courts should give to statutory language, legislative history, precedent, equitable principles, and broader restructuring policy.

themes.name: What are the proper constitutional limits on bankruptcy courts’ ability to alter nondebtor property and contractual rights?
themes.definition: This question evaluates when federal bankruptcy power may impair, release, replace, or otherwise restrict rights held by parties outside the bankruptcy estate.

themes.name: Does concentration of large Chapter 11 cases in Delaware improve bankruptcy administration or encourage harmful forum shopping?
themes.definition: This question investigates the effects of venue selection, geographically remote proceedings, and Delaware’s dominance on fairness, cost, judicial expertise, and stakeholder influence.

themes.name: Is contemporary Chapter 11 shifting too far from negotiated plans toward rapid sales and financially engineered restructurings?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether asset sales and market-oriented transactions are replacing plan-based reorganization in ways that improve speed but weaken creditor participation and distributional safeguards.

themes.name: Do the automatic stay and related collective procedures appropriately displace creditors’ nonbankruptcy enforcement rights?
themes.definition: This question examines when bankruptcy should halt foreclosure, collection, termination, or other external legal actions to protect the estate and coordinate creditor claims.

themes.name: Do bankruptcy financing and administrative-expense priorities preserve value or unfairly dilute prepetition creditors?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether debtor-in-possession financing and payment priority for postpetition expenses are necessary for rescue or permit excessive redistribution away from existing claims.

themes.name: How should bankruptcy estimate and compensate unknown future tort claimants?
themes.definition: This question concerns the representation, valuation, and treatment of contingent or future mass-tort claims when claimants cannot yet identify or participate fully in the proceeding.

themes.name: Should employees and other noncreditor stakeholders receive stronger priority or decision-making rights in corporate reorganizations?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether bankruptcy should privilege wages, employees, public interests, or other noncreditor constituencies over creditor recovery and private contractual entitlements.

themes.name: Should creditors be able to contract around or opt out of bankruptcy’s collective process?
themes.definition: This question examines whether financing agreements, intercreditor contracts, majority-lender provisions, or other private arrangements should control despite bankruptcy’s coordination and equality rules.

themes.name: Do sophisticated repeat players use bankruptcy rights strategically to shift value and control away from weaker constituencies?
themes.definition: This question investigates opportunistic behavior by distressed-debt investors, powerful lenders, attorneys, debtors, and other repeat participants in restructuring proceedings.

themes.name: Does the existing Chapter 11 framework adequately address complex, unconventional, and evolving forms of financial distress?
themes.definition: This question tests whether rules designed for conventional corporate reorganizations remain suitable for complex capital structures, market changes, unusual liabilities, and diverse distressed firms.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy apply a uniform federal priority regime or preserve state-law and other prebankruptcy entitlements?
themes.definition: This question examines the appropriate relationship between federal bankruptcy distribution rules and state-created property, contract, foreclosure, and priority rights.

themes.name: How should bankruptcy success be measured: enterprise value, creditor recovery, speed, fairness, or broader systemic effects?
themes.definition: This question evaluates competing empirical and normative criteria for judging whether a reorganization achieved an effective and legitimate outcome.

themes.name: Does Chapter 11 preserve more going-concern value than liquidation or piecemeal asset sales?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether court-supervised reorganization produces greater economic value for distressed firms and their stakeholders than selling or liquidating the firm’s assets.

themes.name: Should Chapter 11 prioritize creditor wealth maximization over employment, community, and other social objectives?
themes.definition: This question examines whether bankruptcy law should measure success primarily by creditor recoveries or also protect jobs, communities, and broader economic interests.

themes.name: Does the absolute priority rule allocate reorganized-company value fairly and accurately between creditors and equity holders?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether Chapter 11’s priority structure appropriately determines when junior claimants and shareholders may retain value despite unpaid senior claims.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy reorganization be permitted to alter prebankruptcy contractual and secured-creditor priorities?
themes.definition: This question examines whether the collective objectives of bankruptcy justify modifying contractual rights, liens, or priority arrangements established before filing.

themes.name: Do secured-creditor rights over collateral promote efficient recoveries or undermine the collective interests of the bankruptcy estate?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether preserving and enforcing security interests creates value or instead deprives unsecured and junior creditors of a fair collective distribution.

themes.name: Can creditors or private agreements circumvent the Bankruptcy Code’s ordinary distribution and priority rules?
themes.definition: This question investigates when subordination agreements, intercreditor arrangements, transaction structures, or judicial mechanisms improperly enable departures from statutory creditor treatment.

themes.name: Does creditor control after default improve restructuring outcomes or enable coercion and value redistribution?
themes.definition: This question examines whether creditor influence over corporate decisions and reorganization negotiations produces efficient oversight or allows powerful creditors to exploit weaker stakeholders.

themes.name: Does continued control by corporate insiders during financial distress disadvantage creditors?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether debtor-in-possession management and insider participation preserve valuable firm-specific knowledge or create opportunities for managerial and shareholder opportunism.

themes.name: Should bankruptcy courts distinguish legitimate reorganization from strategic or abusive use of bankruptcy?
themes.definition: This question addresses the legal standards courts should use to prevent debtors from filing or structuring proceedings primarily to obtain procedural advantages without resolving genuine financial distress.

themes.name: Do current bankruptcy procedures provide adequate protection against individual creditors extracting value at the expense of the creditor body?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether collective-process rules, avoidance actions, and court supervision effectively prevent creditor races, preferential recoveries, and other forms of individual opportunism.

themes.name: Should financially distressed firms be required or encouraged to file earlier to preserve value?
themes.definition: This question examines whether earlier bankruptcy filing improves reorganization prospects or imposes unnecessary costs and restrictions on firms that might recover outside bankruptcy.

themes.name: Can expedited Section 363 sales properly substitute for a Chapter 11 plan?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether rapid sales of substantially all assets preserve value efficiently or bypass the disclosure, valuation, voting, and oversight protections of plan confirmation.

themes.name: Do the cost, delay, and complexity of traditional Chapter 11 prevent viable firms from reorganizing?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether professional fees, procedural burdens, evidentiary demands, and lengthy proceedings reduce the effectiveness of Chapter 11 for distressed but viable businesses.

themes.name: Does accelerating bankruptcy proceedings promote successful reorganizations or instead encourage inefficient liquidation?
themes.definition: This question examines whether streamlined procedures reduce value-destroying delay or sacrifice meaningful oversight and creditor participation.

themes.name: Does strategic bankruptcy venue selection improve adjudicative efficiency or produce harmful forum shopping?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether debtors’ and creditors’ choices of bankruptcy courts reflect legitimate specialization and efficiency or the pursuit of favorable substantive and procedural outcomes.

themes.name: How should bankruptcy law treat future, contingent, and unknown liabilities such as future tort claims?
themes.definition: This question examines whether existing procedures can identify, value, represent, and compensate claimants whose injuries or obligations are not fully accrued when the bankruptcy begins.

themes.name: When should bankruptcy override or modify nonbankruptcy contractual, state-law, and corporate-law rights?
